At 4:30 p.m. on November 16, 2019, Employee #1 was working on a communication
attaching a holder on a beam in order to frame the house. The opening was
between 30-inches and 40-inches deep. At approximately 8:15 a.m. a Coworker #2
left the area without covering the floor opening to work in the next room
approximately 14 feet away. In that room, Coworker #2 did not return to work
near the opening. Coworker #2 stated he thought someone else would be working
using the opening, but he could not say who and for what. Floor openings were
being created to secure holders to beams which were being installed in order to
strengthen the frame of the house which was common practice. At approximately
2:00 p.m. the employee finished his job assignment installing hangers on the
ceiling. He was concerned about one of the hangers and called Coworker #1 over
to see if he had to redo the hanger. The employee stated one hanger was not
straight. While the employee was walking and speaking to Coworker #1 and
pointing to the ceiling, he stepped right into the floor opening. Neither the
employee nor Coworker #1 were watching where they were walking. Coworker #1
stated opening was created a week prior and it was common practice that openings
were not covered nor attended while they were in use. Employees are expected to
be aware of openings and watch out for them. From this point forward, they
changed procedures to cover every floor opening. The employee fractured his
lower right leg and required hospitalization.
At 8:15 a.m. on February 12, 2019, an employee was moving a 50 foot trailer
loaded with plastic pallets from a staging area to a dock. The employee left the
truck in order to open the trailer doors prior to pulling up to the dock when
the employee discovered the right door was already open in the secured position.
The employee released the latch on the left door unaware that unsecured pallets
were resting against the door. The door flung open and the employee was struck
on the left lower leg by the pallets. He suffered complete breaks to his tibia
and fibia and was hospitalized.

At 12:00 p.m. on July 15, 2019, Employees #1 and #2 and a coworker, employed by
a manufacturer of modular homes, were working at the employer's facility.
Employee #1 was cleaning in the area where a wall of a modular home was being
lifted with the use of an overhead crane.  Employee #2 was working on the other
side of the wall with the coworker, who was operating the crane.  Together they

to the floor and one clamp was installed.  The coworker then slacked down the
slings holding the wall and took the holding pins out.  The coworker left the
site to go to a restroom.  When he returned, the wall, which had not be properly
secured to the modular home, had fallen down on Employees #1 and #2.  Employees
#1 and #2 both required hospitalization.  Employee #1 was treated for a leg
fracture and a head injury and was hospitalized for eight days.  Employee #1 was
treated for multiple fractures and was hospitalized for five days.

conveyor belt when his shirt got caught on a mail bag's zip tie. As a result,
the employee's arm was pulled through an 1.5 inch square opening between the
tail pulley conveyor belt drum guard and the chassis of the belt loader.  A
coworker activated the E-Stop and put the conveyor in reverse  releasing the
employee's arm. The employee's right forearm was seriously injured including
incurring radius and ulna fractures, and he required hospitalization.
At 11:29 p.m. on December 21, 2019, Employee #1 and his supervisor were working
at a two-story residential structure.  Employee #1 was on the first floor roof
and installing a cover on a new Mitsubishi split ductless HVAC unit when he had
a heart attack.  He fell onto the roof's surface.  The supervisor heard Employee
#1's moaning and climbed the ladder onto the roof.  He called for emergency

to the hospital, where he was declared dead.

At 7:20 a.m. on December 10, 2019, an employee was working as an assembler for a
firm that designed and manufactured magnets for scrap metal processing
operations. He was working in the firm's fabrication area. He was cutting small
pieces of fiberglass insulation board on a Lodge & Shipley model 0408 straight
shear. The employee was pushing the material toward the blade, when his finger
went under the guard for one of the hold-downs. The shear cycled, and his finger
was caught under the hold-down. When he tried to pull his hand free, the tip of
his finger was partially amputated. He was treated without hospitalization. The
barrier guard on the shear allowed access to both the hold-downs and the point
of operation. The guard provided on the first hold-down was raised high enough
to allow fingers to pass underneath and into the path of the hold-down. Sight
openings provided in the guard were large enough to reach through to the shear
point. In at least one area, vertical members in the guard were bent, creating a
space that could be reached through to the shear point.

sidewalk.  Employee #1 was killed.
At 7:00 a.m. on August 10, 2020, an employee was laying down plastic at a
strawberry field for fumigation when he collapsed. He was transported to the

At 1:00 p.m. on October 6, 2020, Employee #1, a truck driver employed by a civil

medical services transported the employee to the hospital, where he underwent
multiple surgeries and then was placed on life support.  The employee died
October 7, 2020.  The cause of death was a heart attack.
At 2:00 p.m. on November 11, 2020, an employee had been using a using a Volvo

At approximately 10:15 a.m. on December 7, 2020, an employee contracted the

On December 10, 2020, an employee was working for a framing contractor on a

concussion.
At 2:00 p.m. on August 4, 2020, an employee was struck in the head with a 200
pound beam which had fallen from 10 to 12 feet. The employee was found
unconscious and was still unconscious when first responders arrived. The
employee was hospitalized to treat a concussion.

works roads division was placing compressed air in the tire of a hand cart. The

of the elevated boom and operator basket.  Employee #1 was launched

At 2:00 p.m. on August 25, 2020, Employee #1 was harvesting almonds, and he was
in the process of entering another row at the edge of the almond field.

harvester needed to reenter the field.  A coworker had gone to dump a load of

reverse, he did not see that Employee #1 was at the edge of the orchard trying
to get out, and he struck Employee #1 with the bank out wagon he was operating.
Employee #1 suffered a fracture of the lower left tibia and was hospitalized.
At 3:00 p.m. on November 30, 2020, Employee #1, employed by a construction

and hung up on the inspector when contacted. As a result of the incident, the
employee sustained a partial amputation of the right index finger.   The

An employee was working as a registered nurse (RN) at a nursing care or skilled

At 9:28 p.m. on November 27, 2020, an employee was managing a coin-operated

An employee worked as a Palletizer in the production room of a food

employee was hospitalized for a few days. Information regarding COVID-19 testing

An employee was working as a painter when he began to feeling sick with flu-like

At 9:00 a.m. on January 7, 2020, an employee was tearing down temporary housing
facilities on a oil and gas well site when he complained of shortness of breath
and chest pains. The employee died from a heart attack. There were no biological

At 2:30 p.m. on May 19, 2020, an employee was working for a nationwide chain of
big box stores that sold electrical supplies, plumbing supplies, appliances,
lumber, and so forth. She was working at one of the firm's stores as a customer
service representative. She and a coworker, also a customer service
representative, were replenishing the store's inventory of peat moss. The
coworker was operating a sit-down forklift. The coworker was using the forklift
to retrieve a full pallet of peat moss from the top rack of some storage
shelves. The pallet was approximately 16 feet (4.9 meters) up. The employee was
sitting outside the barricaded zone of a warehouse aisle performing spotting
duties for her coworker. The pile of the bags of peat moss was not stable. As
the coworker removed the full pallet of peat moss, nearly half the bags fell off
the pallet to the ground. The employee crossed over into the barricaded zone to
help pick up the bags from off the ground. There were still some bags elevated
16 feet (4.9 meters) up. Two more bags of peat moss fell off the pallet,
striking the employee in her shoulder and leg. She suffered fractures in her
right ankle and foot. She was hospitalized. The employer reported the accident
to the Division DOSH learned about the accident at approximately 4:44 a.m. on
May 20, 2020. The employer reported the accident within the required timeframe.
The Division arrived at employer's site at approximately 11:00 a.m. on June 5,
2020, to initiate an investigation. A contributing factor to the incident was
the employee's entering the barricaded area of the working aisle. This was
contrary to the training provided by the employer to the employee and the
coworker. No accident-related citations were to be issued.
At 7:45 a.m. on May 28, 2020, Employee #1, employed by a construction company,
was working from an elevated platform and engaged in forming work at the

At 7:45 a.m. on June 2, 2020, Employee # 1, a laborer, was working in a field,
removing stakes that support almond trees from the ground. He collapsed and was

He was not using any other equipment. DOSH was notified the same day at 1:54
p.m. OSH medical confirmed that the illness was not heat related. No violations
were issued. Employee # 1's family reported that the employee died of a heart
attack.
At 2:00 p.m. on February 10, 2020, an employee working for on a wooden pallet
manufacturer was using a pallet knotcher trying to clear a jam when machine

suffered and electrocution and was killed.
At 10:30 a.m. on June 17, 2020, an employee working as for an explosives
manufacturer was operating press 8 when the product jammed and caused a
deflagration. The employee burned his face and arms in the resulting flash fire

At 1:00 p.m. on April 22, 2020, an employee was looking at the carburetor.  The
employee stuck his hand under the mower deck and amputated a finger. The
employee was hospitalized.
At 10:30 a.m. on June 11, 2020, an employee was assisting the foreman with
removing the lid/cap to a chemical tote. The foreman applied heat from a propane

employee sustained chemical and flash fire burns over 30-40% of his body. The
employee was hospitalized.
At 2:00 p.m. on June 14, 2020, an employee became infected with COVID-19 and
died.
At 12:00 p.m. on June 16, 2020, Employee #1 was on telework status, but stopped

At 2:30 p.m. on June 7, 2020 (the worksheet said June 6), an employee was
working for a firm that made single-use hygiene and health products. The
employee was working in the facility's location PM 11, the finish end. He was
tending to a Cameron model 450 slitter/rewinder. Two web breaks in close
succession on this slitter/rewinder necessitated removing the broken paper from
the roll ("pulling slab") and rethreading the machine to continue production.
Pulling a slab was a common procedure in the event of a web break at the
rewinder. To remove the slab, the employee placed the machine in crawl mode at
the human-machine interface (HMI) control panel. The employee and a coworker
entered an interlocked safety enclosure (safety cell) around the rewinder. With
the machine running in a crawl mode of about 15 meters per minute, (49 feet per
minute) and no one at the HMI control panel, the employee and his coworker began
pulling the slab. As the employee was tucking the paper back into the infeed nip
between the bed roll and the finished roll, his left hand got caught in the nip.
His arm was pulled in up to his elbow. It was crushed. The coworker left the
safety cell and got to the HMI control panel, where he reversed the roll
direction, freeing the employee's arm. A second coworker called the guard shack
to notify 911, while a third coworker wrapped the employee's arm in paper and
comforted the employee until EMS arrived. It took about 20 minutes for emergency
medical personnel to respond. The employee was hospitalized. He was expected to
regain full use of his arm. The delay in response was attributed to the
procedure in contacting off-site emergency medical personnel. Plant procedure
was to contact security at the guard shack. Security then called in the
emergency. A plant nurse was at the facility every other day from Monday through
Friday, but the facility ran 24 hours per day, including weekends. There was no
onsite emergency response team when the incident occurred.

energized circuit and was electrocuted.
At 1:00 p.m. on October 19, 2020, an employee working as a feed mill operator
for a grain merchant was running corn through a roller mill. The mill was an
automatic machine that consisted of three sets of rollers. The employee observed
the milled corn and was not satisfied with its grind consistency. The gap
between the roller sets produced the desired grain consistency. As the grain
fell through the rollers, the rollers would grind the grain. The rollers could
be adjusted from the exterior of the milling machine to achieve the desired
grind. The employee turned off the machine at the control panel and then
proceeded to remove the bottom metal cover once the belts and pulleys had
stopped moving. The employee reached into the mill past the second roller set to
the bottom rollers in order to check the gap between the set. The bottom rollers
were still moving and pulled his right hand into the gap. The employee received
medical treatment for four partially amputated fingers but was not hospitalized.
At 4:15 a.m. on October 24, 2020, an employee working as a supervisor for the
U.S. Mint was operating a table saw cutting a piece of wood. The employee struck
his hand with the blade. He received medical treatment without hospitalization
for an amputated finger.

working for a heating and air conditioning contractor, were preparing to install
a new concentric HVAC unit. Employee #1 was attempting to set the curb in place
on the roof of a commercial building. The owner called coworker #1 down from the
roof, and coworker #2 followed, leaving Employee #1 on the roof alone. Employee
#1 fell through a fiberglass skylight approximately 19 feet 8 inches to the
concrete ground. Employee #1 was hospitalized and treated for three broken bones
in the back, a broken left leg, a broken right hand, and a fractured left hand.
At 5:15 a.m. on October 26, 2020, an employee working as a machine operator for
a refractory was performing maintenance on the Sacmi Press Dryer Exit Elevator 3
in Plant 1. A counterweight chain on the elevator was not working properly. The
belt broke and the operator shutdown the equipment. The employee proceeded to
adjust the counterweight chain. The employee bypassed the interlock system and
tagged out the equipment to start performing maintenance. The counterweight
chain on the elevator dryer table contains a counterbalance weight. The employee
placed his hand onto the chain, placing his fingers between the sprocket and the
chain. Due to the employee moving the slacked chain onto the sprocket, the
counterbalance weight shifted and dropped. The shift in the chain caused the
employee's fingers to be caught between the sprocket and the chain. The employer
hazardous energy control procedures did not identify mechanical energy (gravity)
as a hazard. The employee received medical treatment without hospitalization for
an amputated finger.
At 9:32 a.m. on October 3, 2020, an employee was operating a pacer (stand-up)
forklift (Raymond Forklift, Model: 425-C30TT, Serial Number: 425-13-37439) in
order to bring empty pallets towards the bay doors of the facility.  As stated

was in place. As the employee was nearing the storage rack at a speed he felt
was uncomfortable, the employee stuck out his foot as a reaction to brace for
impact between the forklift and the storage rack guard. The employee stated he
knew he shouldn't have placed his foot outside of the forklift, but his
immediate reaction was to react in that manner. The employee was trained and
certified by the company in the operation of the forklift.  Maintenance tests
were conducted to determine if there was any malfunction of the forklift.  All
results determined there was no malfunctioning by the equipment. The employee
suffered a crushed left foot with exposed tissues and bone, resulting in a
surgical amputation of the left leg below the left knee.  The employee was
hospitalized.

on the top of a scale house. During the fall, the employee struck the supporting

injuries and was hospitalized for treatment.

At 6:00 a.m. on October 8, 2020, Employee #1 was ripping a narrow door jam on
the Altendorf F45 sliding table saw.  Employee #1 was feeding the narrow piece

Employee #1 struck his right hand and fingers against the saw blade, leading to

At 10:00 a.m. on October 13, 2020, an employee working as a groundskeeper for a
forest district was driving a John Deere Gator Utility Vehicle (UTV) on a golf
course. The employee was driving down a hill when the left rear tire went flat
causing the vehicle to swerve violently off the path. The UTV flipped over on a
bunker bank and landed in a sand trap rolling over onto the employee. The
employee was hospitalized to treat a broken left hip and fractured shoulder.
At 10:30 a.m. on October 13, 2020, an employee working as a machine operator for
an oilfield services company was steam washing a tank. The tank had formerly
held produced water from oil and gas operations. A flash fire occurred and
struck the employee in the upper body. The employee was hospitalized to treat
3rd degree burns to his hands and 2nd degree burns to his face and ears.
An employee working on a food production line contracted COVID-19, potentially
from a co-worker on the same line. The employee was hospitalized and died on
July 22, 2020, from complications of COVID-19.
At 4:15 p.m. on August 31, 2020, an employee was working for an internet service
provider. He installed and repaired equipment. In this incident, he was working
as a field technician. He was working on radio relay receivers and transmitters
located above the top of a silo. To access the equipment, the employee had
climbed up a set of stairs on a fixed ladder with a cage. The ladder and cage
were over 35 feet (10.7 meters) tall. The employee was working at an elevation.
He was walking toward a taller relay device to adjust it manually. The employee
needed to cross the ladder opening in order to reach a platform to get to the
relay. The relay was on the left side of the ladder opening, and the employee
was on the right side of the opening. The employee was looking at his cellphone,
and he walked into the ladder opening and fell. The employee fell onto a catwalk
below the fixed ladder that he had ascended to reach the platform. He suffered a
full-thickness laceration to his left inner upper arm, and lacerations near his
left wrist and the right side of his chin. He was hospitalized. Drugs were found
at the area where the employee stayed after he descended the silo stairs while
waiting for emergency services.
At 3:00 p.m. on May 7, 2020,  Employee #1, was operating a 2019 Honda ATV, Model
TRX500FM6. At the time, there were six employees on ATVs moving a herd of 120
cattle approximately 2 miles down the road to a different lot, when cattle got
away from the employees and entered an alfalfa field that was cut.  Employee #1
had to turn his ATV around and go back down the road to an access point at the
end of the field; then, he drove through the field while several other employees
dismounted their ATVs and entered the field on foot.  Employee #1 was looking to
his left as he approached the rear of the herd, when a cow stopped in front of
him.  Employee #1 looked back towards his path of travel, saw the cow in his
path and took steps to avoid striking the cow, causing the ATV to turn over onto
him. The employees were not wearing helmets while operating the ATVs on the day
of the accident.  The employer has an Employee Safety Manual that provides
safety guidelines for ATV safety, including the requirement to never operate an
ATV without an approved motorcycle helmet. Employee #1 suffered serious injuries
to his ribs and a lung, with non-serious injuries to the head.  Employee #1 was
transported to Kaiser Medical Center in Vacaville and was treated for his
injuries, which lasted for longer than 24 hours.
At 11:30 p.m. on October 4, 2020, an employee was using a pair of snip pliers to
remove the sprue plug from the Cincinnati Milicron Mold Machine #14 during the
machine warmup process. When the sprue plug was removed, the pressure inside the
machine caused molten resin to be ejected onto the employee's left hand and arm.
The employee was hospitalized to treat second degree burns to the left arm and
hand.
At 6:00 p.m. on October 1, 2020, an employee working for a retail establishment
was feeding wood into a Weinig Hydromat 22 A L 6 Head Moulder. While feeding the
wood into the Moulder the wood jammed. The employee walked over to the location
on the machine where the wood moves under the roller when noticed a wood strip
was stuck on the rail. She pulled on the wood to get it off the rail when a
rotor turned on. The part snagged her gloves and pulled her left hand toward a
point of operation. The employee amputated her index, middle and ring fingers
and received medical treatment without hospitalization.
At 2:00 p.m. on August 31, 2020, an employee was working for a nationwide chain
of retail stores that sold arts and crafts and hobby supplies. She was working
at one of the firm's retail outlets, located in a shopping center. She was
working as a retail or inventory clerk. She was using a 6-ft (1.8-m) stepladder
to take inventory and see what product needed to be ordered, apparently in the
fabric department. She was climbing the stepladder, and she missed a step. She
fell to the floor and suffered a fracture and contusion to her leg and head. The
employee was transported via ambulance to a medical center. She was
hospitalized. There were no witnesses to the incident, and no video was
available. A walkaround inspection of the store's fabric department was
conducted on October 16, 2020.
At 5:25 a.m. on September 22, 2020, an employee was working for a firm that
provided general warehousing and storage. He was operating a stand-up pallet
jack in a warehouse aisle. He was approaching a place where his aisle crossed
another aisle. A coworker operating a sit-down powered industrial truck in the
cross aisle was approaching that intersection as well. Views in that
intersection were obstructed. The coworker did not slow down his industrial
truck, and he collided with the stand-up pallet jack that the employee was
operating. The employee's foot was caught between the pallet jack and the
forklift. The employee suffered a fracture, and he was hospitalized.
At 12:34 a.m. on August 31, 2020, an employee was working as a full-time
permanent employee of a temporary staffing agency. She had been sent to work at
a processing facility for food and grocery distribution. The workers there
prepared products for shipment. The employee was walking through the warehouse
looking for order items. She was in an aisle between the candy and freezer
areas. Her supervisor was engaged in supervisory duties, away the scene of the
incident. An employee of the firm that owned the warehouse was operating a
powered industrial truck (PIT), which was also said to be a forklift. The
operator did not look in his direction of travel, and his truck struck the
employee, crushing her foot. The employee was transported to a community
hospital, where she was hospitalized for three days. The employee was
transferred to another hospital, where she was hospitalized for two weeks. The
employee suffered the loss of all toes on her left foot after they were crushed
by the wheel of the powered industrial truck or forklift. The wording of the
narrative suggested that the toes were surgically amputated, not traumatically
amputated in the incident. The employer failed to report the serious injury to
DOSH and was not in compliance with the requirements of T8CCR �342(a). The DOSH
investigator arrived on site at about 1:00 p.m. on October 16, 2020. The owner
of the warehouse was cited for a serious accident-related violation for
�3650(t)(12). The incident would not have occurred had the operator of the PIT
or forklift been looking in the direction of travel to ensure a clear path. A
similar incident occurred at the same warehouse three weeks later. See
investigation 130440 and UPA 1671856.
An employee was performing housekeeping duties in a nursing home when she was
exposed to residents and coworkers who were infected with COVID-19. The employee
contracted COVID-19 and subsequently died at 10:15 a.m. on June 28, 2020.
At 3:00 a.m. on October 13, 2020, Employee #1 was performing media blasting on
structural steel at an auto care center to clean and prepare it for coating.
After about an hour of blasting, the nozzle became clogged, causing the employee
to lose control. During the incident, the employee's left hand slid in front of
the blasting nozzle, and pressurized garnet-sand media entered the hand. The
employee sustained a high-pressure laceration and abrasion to the left thumb and
was hospitalized for treatment.
At 2:30 p.m. on September 22, 2020, an employee was working for a nationwide
chain of stores that sold nursery, garden, and farm supplies and clothing for
the outdoors. He was a purchasing manager. He was working at one of the firm's
retail outlets. He was manually moving a log splitter form the back of the
retail store to the product display located just outside the front of the store.
As he was pulling the log splitter, its back left tire hit the corner of a
pallet. The log splitter's jack pin was not seated, so when the tire hit the
corner of the pallet, the log splitter tipped forward. The middle finger of the
employee was treated without hospitalization.
At 2:45 a.m. on October 7, 2020, an employee was moving materials with a
forklift.  The employee raised the load to 10 feet, made a turn, and the
forklift tipped over.  The forklift fell on the employee.  The employee was
hospitalized to treat a fractured pelvis and internal bleeding.
At 6:50 a.m. on October 2, 2020, an employee working as a maintenance helper for
a chicken egg producer was adjusting a sensor on the egg grading machine. As the
employee was adjusting the sensor he contacted the chain and sprocket with his
left. The employee amputated two fingers on his left hand and was hospitalized.
At 10:45 a.m. on October 5, 2020, Employee #1 was using a tractor to spread lime
along a hillside.  As Employee #1 was maneuvering along the hillside, going
towards the top, the tractor got into a rut. The tractor started to go
backwards, and despite hitting the brakes and attempting to correct the
direction, the tractor proceeded to roll down the hill. Employee #1 was
hospitalized to treat a spinal fracture, fractured right leg, broken right
clavicle, broken ribs and an injured right eye.
At 6:45 a.m. on September 30, 2020, an employee was working as a shop helper for
a cabinet manufacturer. The employee was being trained by Coworker #1 (machine
operator/trainer). It was the employee's third day working at the location. In
the previous days, Coworker #1 was showing the employee how to safely operate
the electric table saws and other equipment around the shop. Currently, Coworker

66 10-inch Tilting Arbor Saw. According to Coworker #2 (operations manager) they
had just cut a 3/4-inch composite wood board on the table saw when Coworker #1
briefly stepped away to take care of another task. After the cut was complete,
the employee allegedly used his gloved right pinkie finger to attempt to flick
away a piece of residual wood from the left side of the rotating blade. As a
result, the employee sustained a laceration to his fingertip through the glove
when his hand contacted the sawblade. The employee was transported in a private
vehicle to the hospital, where he was treated and released within two hours and
reported back to work the same day.
At 3:00 a.m. on October 7, 2020, an employee working as a carpenter for a civil
engineering contractor was lowering lumber forms from a riprap retaining wall
(ramp). While the employee was lowering a form to a coworker located at ground
level, the employee tripped over a cable and fell approximately 8 feet to the
lower level. The employee was not wearing fall protection. The employee was
hospitalized to treat a lumbar fracture.
At 9:30 a.m. on October 4, 2020, an employee was clearing a jam. The machine
started while the employee's arm was inside the machine. The employee was
hospitalized to treat a fractured and lacerated arm.
At 2:20 p.m. on June 12, 2020, Employee #1 and a coworker were called to clean
the SFW wash tank. Employee #1 was using a pressurized hose and water to clean
out the valve. Employee #1 reached into the valve opening to remove a rock
fragment, and the valve inadvertently closed and crushed his right-hand fingers.
Employee #1 was transported to the occupational clinic and treated for his
injury. On July 1, 2020, Employee #1 had surgery and part of his middle finger
was amputated.  Employee #1 was hospitalized.
At 9:30 a.m. on October 1, 2020, an employee was working for a farm merchant
wholesaler and was inside a grain bin. The bin auger and sweeper energized at
the time. While in the bin, the employee contacted the auger with his right leg.
The employee was hospitalized to treat an amputation to his leg below the knee.
An employee was working in the COIVD-19 unit as a certified nursing assistant
when she was tested for COVID-19 by the employer and sent home after a positive
test on September 30, 2020. The employee was at home when she died due to from
complications of a COVID-19 infection on October 7, 2020.
At 4:45 p.m. on October 7, 2020, an employee was on standby 30 feet from a
coworker in case the use of a pump truck was needed. The coworker was working on
ruptures, spraying 150 degree Fahrenheit leachate. The employee suffered first
and second degree burns to the neck, chest, abdomen and arms from the hot
leachate and was hospitalized.
At 1:30 p.m. on September 19, 2020, Employee #1 was marking underground
utilities at a worksite. A drunk driver drove behind the jersey wall and struck
the employee. The employee sustained abrasions and a fracture from the impact.
The employee was hospitalized for treatment of the injuries.
At 1:00 p.m. on April 21, 2020, Employee #1 was replacing a ballast in a light
fixture on a live circuit.  Employee #1 was standing 7-feet up a 24-foot
extension ladder that was leaning against the wall.  Employee #1 stated that
upon connecting the power leads, he noticed there was an arcing due to poor

fractures of his left ankle and was hospitalized for approximately 3 days.
Two employees (Employee #1 and Employee #2) were working at a nursing care or

day, on August 21, 2020. That employee died on October 4, 2020.  Employee #2
tested positive for COVD-19 on September 1, 2020. That employee was hospitalized

At 5:00 p.m. on October 7, 2020, an employee was driving a golf cart to ensure

limb that fell on the cart and crushed it. The employee died due to head trauma.
At 7:45 a.m. on October 5, 2020, an employee was climbing a ladder. The employee
felt ill and fell from the ladder approximately 6-8 feet.  The employee suffered
a broken leg, which resulted in an amputation.  The employee was hospitalized.
At 10:00 a.m. on October 6, 2020, Employee #1 was working for a residential

panels. Employee #1 fell through a skylight. Employee #1 suffered a fractured
neck, concussion, pelvic fracture and internal bleeding.  Employee #1 was
hospitalized.
At 5:30 a.m. on October 1, 2020, an employe working as a maintenance technician
for a wood products manufacturer was changing a roller on a roll coating
machine. The employee was using a screwdriver in order to align the new roller
with the connection point on the machine. The screwdriver slipped causing the
roller to slip and catch the employee's left-hand thumb. The employee lacerated
his thumb and required hospitalization.

associated cases within a few weeks. One employee died on June 8, 2020, and

At 11:30 a.m. on August 26, 2020, an employee was pulling wire from an
electrical cabinet. At some point, the employee made contact with a live wire or
other live electrical component in the electrical cabinet. The employee was
killed by electrocution.
At 3:30 p.m. on April 15, 2020, an employee was working on a building and was

An employee was working as a cellar worker at a winery and last worked on
pelican clip showed lanyard deployment.
At 2:30 p.m. on May 5, 2020, Employee #1 was working for a framing contractor.
Employee #1 was framing the second floor of a residential building. Employee #1
was holding a wall, when a gust of wind caused the employee to lose his balance
and fall.  Employee fell approximately 4 feet onto a fence then fell 6 feet to
the ground. Employee #1 suffered a laceration to the lower back and was

At 3:00 p.m. on October 16, 2020, Employee # 1 was changing out 80 amp breakers

At 2:50 p.m. on April 25, 2020, an employee was standing in a fruit bin on the
forks of a forklift, that was being used as an elevated platform. The fruit bin

At 10:30 a.m. on November 23, 2020, an employee was jacking up an extruder
machine so that slides could be placed under it.  The slides were to be used for

the die fell onto the employee who was operating the jack. The employee was

At 9:00 a.m. on November 24, 2020, Employee #1 and coworkers, employed by a
scaffold company, were dismantling a five-level stair tower scaffold at the

At 2:45 p.m. on November 24, 2020, Employee #1, a Laborer employed by a small
construction company and a coworker, the company's owner, were building a new

At 6:15 a.m. on August 8, 2020, an employee was cleaning a conveyor belt. When
the employee was cleaning under the conveyor, the employee came in contact with
a different conveyor belt. This resulted in fractured right wrist. The employee
was taken to the local hospital by ambulance. The employee was hospitalized. The
cause of the fractured right wrist was the conveyor.
At 2:45 a.m. on November 14, 2020, Employee #1, a 47-year-old male packaging
technician, was assisting a machine operator in fixing a registration issue with
the Sig Wrapper (packaging machine) that was preventing product from running
through the machine properly. The technician was using his left hand to manually

pinched between two exposed rollers on the tucker. The employee suffered a

At approximately 7:40 P.M. on May 26, 2020, an employee, working for a building
contractor, was completing construction at a commercial building using a ladder.

the ground. The employee was hospitalized and treated for a fractured left
ankle.
At 9:00 a.m. on July 9, 2020, an employee was sharpening a knife using a steel
rod in the seafood section of a grocery store. The employee was holding the

underwent surgery for nerve, tendon and ligament injuries to the right hand.
At 11:40 a.m. on October 21, 2020, an employee working as a machine operator for
a fabricated metals manufacturer was inserting a piece of metal into the
machine. The employee caught his glove on a metal roller causing his left hand
to be pulled into the machine. The employee amputated his index and middle
fingers and was hospitalized needing surgery.
At 10:30 a.m. on November 23, 2020, an employee was on a 12-foot ladder wiping
and cleaning the driver side of a trash collecting truck getting it ready for
painting. The employee fell from the ladder and suffered blunt force trauma
injuries to his head and neck. The employee died of complications from blunt
force injuries to the head and neck.
At 6:21 a.m. on September 17, 2020, Employee #1 and Employee #2, both working on
a unit substation HVL switch, removed the backside feeder panels and began
wiping down the 3-phase 12kV lines. While performing this task, Employee #1 made
contact with the C-phase of the live line, resulting in an electrical shock. The
employee became stuck to the component. Employee #2 quickly grabbed Employee #1
and pulled him off the live component. Employee #1 and Employee #2 suffered
second- and third-degree burns and internal thermal injuries. Emergency services
were called, and both employees were transported to the hospital for admission
and treatment.
At 10:41 p.m. on November 11, 2020, an employee was placing labels on boxes.  A
coworker was transporting a load of vacuums on a forklift that was two pallets
high. After making a right turn, the material began to wobble and started to
fall. The employee was facing the opposite direction of the falling load and the

At 12:50 or 1:00 p.m. on December 19, 2019, an employee was working at a firm
that manufactured cheese. She was a machine operator. She was working alone in
the production room. She was cleaning the mold machine. For the mold machine to
be cleaned, it was necessary that parts move. As the employee hand washed the
machine with hot water, she would turn it on and off. With the machine running,
the employee was hand washing the screw conveyor. The thumb of her right glove
became caught on the machine's conveyor belt. To free her caught right thumb and
glove from the conveyor belt, the employee lifted the mold machine's safety
cage. This move shut the mold machine off. She asked a coworker for help. To
free the employee's glove from the mold machine, the employee and her coworker
lowered the machine's safety cage. This move activated the screw conveyor. The
conveyor pulled the employee's right arm into the body of the machine. The fire
department was call. Rescue personnel removed the employee's right arm from the
machine and transported her to the hospital. The employee underwent surgery for
fractures to her right arm and thumb as well as nerve damage to her right arm.
She was hospitalized. She was admitted on December 19, 2019, and discharged on
December 27, 2019. The fire department reported the incident to the Long Beach
CAL-OSHA office later on the day of the incident. The employer did not report
the incident on a timely basis and thus did not meet the requirements of 342(a).
On January 28, 2020, the division conducted an investigation of the incident.
The employer to did not provide the employee with an extension cleaning tool
that would have prevented her from placing her hand in the immediate area of the
energized screw conveyor. Employees were not familiar with the safe use and
maintenance of such tools, methods, or means by thorough training.

An employee, who worked in a receiving department sorting mail and entering it

At 8:00 a.m. on July 6, 2020, an employee was driving a garbage truck when he
was involved in a roll over accident. The employee incurred a broken pelvis in
the accident and was hospitalized.
At 3:00 p.m. on November 3, 2020, an employee was operating a Raymond Model
DSD50R Powered Industrial Truck (PIV) to dump a container of trash into a
dumpster. The employee was standing between the mast and cab attempting to push
the container from the forks when he bumped into the control levers causing the

At 12:00 p.m. on September 18, 2020, an employee was performing his normal tasks
of running metal cutting lathes and presses. The employee ended up with two
metal slivers in his foot that already had a mild infection.  The employee was
hospitalized.
At 11:00 a.m. on July 10, 2020, an employee was working for a manufacturer of
ready-mix concrete. He was driving a concrete truck. He was found unresponsive
next to his concrete truck. He had apparently suffered a heart attack. He was
dead. His death was later attributed to a cardiovascular event and possible
complication with cancer.
An employee was working as a certified nursing aide in the dementia unit of a
nursing home when she tested positive for COVID-19. The employee's last day of
work was April 20, 2020, and she died on May 27, 2020.
At 10:45 a.m. on November 2, 2020, Employee #1 and a coworker, employed by a
construction company, were working at a new five-story multifamily residential
building, a multi-employer construction project.  They were installing OSB
(oriented strand board) engineered wood panels to the exterior of the building.
Employee #1 was working inside the building on the fourth level, taking
measurements and making cuts in 4 by 8 foot sheets of OSB.  His coworker was
safety laser scanner system on all three CNC tube benders in similar

system created unmonitored areas near the point of operation that would not
prevent employee access. Additionally, the placement of the safety laser scanner

manufacturer's operations manual per ISO13855 (2005) and IEC61496-3 (2008) when
the operator was working near or with the machine interface or two hand control.
Employees did not receive training on the safety laser scanner systems. They
were not required to test them routinely. After the incident covered by this

An employee was working as a volunteer fire fighter for a borough's fire
department. Somehow, he was infected with severe acute respiratory syndrome
coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2), the virus that causes COVID-19. At 10:00 p.m. on
April 17, 2020, he died.
At 2:05 p.m. on October 13, 2020, Employee #1, employed by a water and sewer
line construction company, was installing a 42-inch ductile pipe inside two 10
feet by 24 feet stacked trench boxes inside an 18 feet deep trench.  The trench
wall collapsed, fell through the spreader bar, and struck Employee #1 from
behind.  The employee's body was forced against the ductile pipe.  Employee #1
sustained traumatic injuries and was killed.
At 2:30 p.m. on October 8, 2020, Employee #1 was operating a Grizzly 12-inch
table saw. Employee #1 was making cross-cuts, reducing the wood stock in length
for cabinets and was sweeping wood scrap away from the surface of the table saw.
Employee #1 made contact with the spinning blade.  The hood guard on the table
saw did not lay flush to the surface of the table, which resulted in an
amputation to the three middle fingers of the right hand.  Employee #1 was
hospitalized.  The hood guard of the Grizzly 12-inch table saw was not in
compliance, as it was raised approximately 9/16 of an inch above the working
surface.
At 12:00 noon on October 1, 2020, an employee was on a routine route collecting
recyclable material. The employee stepped off the recycling truck and was struck
by a passing vehicle. The employee was hospitalized due to blunt force trauma to
the abdomen and chest and subsequently died.
At 9:30 a.m. on October 23, 2019, an employee was power washing a metal duct
near the ceiling of the first floor. The employee had fall protection on but was
not tied off and fell from the scissors lift to the concrete floor below.  The
employee was killed from blunt force trauma to the head.
At 1:15 p.m. on October 8, 2020, an employee was removing bolts from the diving
door of a submarine, using an air driven impact wrench. When the employee
removed the final bolt, the door swung down, pushing the impact wrench down on
his hand, and his thumb got pinched between the impact wrench and the support
beam under the submarine. X-rays revealed some bone loss to the left thumb,
classifying the injury as an amputation.  The employee was treated without
hospitalization.

farm. The company produced dairy products. The employee was in the dairy's cow
hospital, moving cattle. He was near a tote or storage tank that contained "a
large quantity" of a solution of 37 percent formaldehyde. The UPA said that the
solution was 35 percent formaldehyde and 10 percent methanol. The methanol was
present to stabilize the formaldehyde. The formaldehyde was used on one shift
per week. As the tote was being filled, it fell over or was knocked over. The
UPA said the tote was overfilled. Some of the formaldehyde solution splashed
onto the employee. The employee was hospitalized for observation. The employer
had not provided conveniently located quick drench showers.
At 4:35 p.m. on September 30, 2020, an employee was working as a laborer for a
food manufacturer had experienced a jam in a grinder for the third time. The

machinery frame. The employee lacerated his right index finger without bone loss
and required medical treatment without hospitalization.

down and off of the ramp. The employee jumped from the forklift resulting in the
rollover protection landing on his leg. The employee was hospitalized to treat a
crushed leg.
At 12:00 a.m. on October 6, 2020, an employee was using a machine. The belt came
off the track. The employee removed the safety device with the machine off, to
put back the belt. His right index finger was caught between the pully and the
belt, resulting in an amputation.  The employee was treated without
hospitalization.

At 11:15 a.m. on October 6, 2020, an employee had his right fingertip caught and

The employee sustained severe abdominal and chest injuries and later died.
At 11:40 a.m. on October 21, 2020, an employee was infected with COVID-19 and
was hospitalized.

southwest side of the conveyor. The conveyor was energized and shocked Employee
# 1. He was stuck between a wooden support beam and the conveyor for
approximately 22 seconds, as he was shocked. Employee # 1 was initially
hospitalized with electrical shock injuries on October 3, 2020. He died on

coworker closed the door and turned the machine on while the employee was inside
the belt area of the machine. The employee's hands were drawn into the moving
belt. The employee's right hand was crushed and subsequently amputated. The
employee also sustained contusions to the left fingers. The employee was
hospitalized.
At 7:10 p.m. on May 7, 2020, Employee # 1 was driving a Chevrolet pickup truck
which is used to treat severe carbon monoxide poisoning. After reviewing the
employee's medical records, OSHA's Salt Lake City laboratory was able to
determine the levels of carbon monoxide exposure and extrapolate an 8-hour TWA
of carbon monoxide exposure. The employee was exposed to CO levels of 115.7 ppm.
The employee and the supervisor both worked beneath an exhaust hood designed to
remove toxic gases including, but not limited to, carbon monoxide, which was
emitted after the annealing process. The amount of COHb in the employee's blood
reached a calculated peak level of 33.2 percent. At the calculated peak level of
33.2 percent, symptoms in health adults would include severe headache,
dizziness, nausea, vomiting, and cognitive impairment.
At 8:30 a.m. on June 9, 2020, Employee #1 was operating a riding mower, when he
observed a coworker having difficulty with his Toro 21 push mower. The coworker
had released the blade activation bar; however, the cables had been stretched
out.  When the coworker released the bar, it did not shut down the moving mower
blades. Employee #1 came over to help. He went to flip the mower over but did
not know the blades were still engaged, and his fingers came in contact with the
moving blades. Employee #1 sustained amputations to three of his fingers and was
hospitalized.

tank.  When the coworker returned to the area, he found the employee on the
platform, not moving, with his hoodie caught around the shaft of the machine.
The coworker climbed up the ladder and pulled the cord to stop machine.
Emergency services were called, and the employee pronounced dead at the scene.

landscaping service was working in the front yard of a private residence working

ground while two coworkers were trimming branches above the employee in the
tree.  One of the branches being cut fell to the ground, bounced off the ground
and struck the employee in the head. The employee was hospitalized to treat
facial fractures.
At 11:37 a.m. on October 8, 2020, an employee working as a construction laborer
for a structural concrete contractor was performing trenching in the backyard of
a residence.  The employee was instructed by the employer to cut a tree root
located inside the trench. The employee was using a Dewalt hand grinder and a
Skilsaw. While the employee was cutting the tree root, the 4-inch sawblade
jammed and kicked back and struck him in the right foot. The employee was
hospitalized to treat an amputated toe.
An employee was engaged in assisting with the response to a wildland fire in the
San Joaquin Valley between August 23 and August 28, 2020. The employee was
engaged in wildland fire activities that involved disturbing soils with various
tools. Dirt was also being stirred up by strong winds. The employee was exposed
to Coccidioides, a fungus which lives in dirt, and developed coccidioidomycosis
(Valley Fever) and pneumonia. The employee was hospitalized at St. Mary Medical
Center in Apple Valley and Kaiser Permanente Hospital in Ontario. Using
NIOSH-approved respiratory protection with particulate filters rated as N95,
N99, N100, P100, or HEPA may have prevented the exposure to Coccidioides.  The
Division found no violations, as the employer was unaware of the hazard.
At 3:15 p.m. on July 15, 2020, an employee was pulling a stack of milk crates
off a floor level drag conveyor when his foot slipped into the unguarded
conveyor drive. The floors are kept wet to allow the stacks to easily slide
along the floors.  The employee caught his right foot between the floor chain
and the guide rollers crushing it. The employee was hospitalized, and his leg
was later amputated below the knee.
At 9:15 a.m. on May 12, 2020, Employee #1 was working for a steel erection
contractor.  A steel beam was being placed/seated into another steel member for
a new commercial structure.  The two members did not fit together properly
resulting in the beam falling and striking Employee #1.  Employee #1 suffered
contusions and a leg fracture.  Employee #1 was hospitalized.

injection mold, his left hand was between the two molds, as he used an air
ratchet to unbolt the right-side mold.  The coworker was using a stepladder,
where he was unhooking the water and plastic lines that feed to the injection
molds. The coworker accidentally tripped the high-pressure limit switch that
actuated 100 p.s.i. air, causing the injection molds to slam together.  Employee
#1's hand was crushed in between the two molds.  The machine was not turned off
and not locked out. Employee #1 suffered a crushed left hand and broken bones
and was hospitalized.
On October 7, 2020, Employee #1, the owner of a construction company, was
working with employees to build a new road.  Employee #1 was operating a D6

down the hill.  Employee #1 was ejected from the dozer's cab.  Employee #1 was
killed.

manufacturer was taping up a new core roll on a calendar line winder. After he
had removed the full roll, the employee placed a new role and core onto the
winder. He then started up the winder and began to place tape onto the core with

additional injuries to his feet, knees, and torso. At the time of the incident,
the safety pressure mat was pushed up underneath the machine and was not in the
proper place. Additionally, it was found that this mat would not have stopped
the roll from spinning and was actually to there to prevent the winder from
indexing.
At 12:30 p.m. on September 23, 2020, an employee was inside a truck mounted
attenuator in the gore zone of a highway near the exit when he stepped out of
the truck. As he walked on the highway, he was struck by a moving vehicle. The
employee suffered multiple traumatic injuries and was killed.
At 8:45 a.m. on May 18, 2020, an employee was working for a grain elevator. He
drove heavy trucks. He was at a customer's farm. He was walking on the top of a
and he was pronounced deceased at the accident scene. The employee sustained a
fractured skull, cervical spine, and ribs as well as multiple internal injuries.
At 3:00 p.m. on September 18, 2020, an employee was hanging a dye on a printing
press. The employee attempted to restart a stalled printing press. The
employee's hand was on a moving piston part, which caught his hand. The
employee's finger was amputated in the printing press.  The employee was
hospitalized.
At 11:45 a.m. on October 2, 2020, an employee working as a senior extruder
operator for a plastic products manufacturer was preparing to clean the middle
roller on the roll stand of a P4 Extruder. The machine was a was a Processing
Technologies International Model RJU601220 (serial number 16532/4329) Plastic

shift at his career fire department and then proceeded to answer calls with his
volunteer fire department where he spent the day clearing downed trees and other
emergency calls in response to a tropical storm. The employee was found
unresponsive at his home in and was transported to a local hospital but was
unable to be revived. The employee died due to cardiac arrest.
An employee was working at a firm that processed meat from carcasses. It was a
meatpacker. The employee had started a pre-scheduled vacation. He was to return
to work in the second week of October.  On October 3, 2020, he died of COVID-19.
At 3:00 p.m. on October 5, 2020, Employee #1, employed by an electrical
contractor, was working at a multi-employer construction project, a commercial
warehouse building.  He was climbing down the fixed stair ladder of a JLG
Electric Scissor Lift, Model 3246-E2, Serial Number 0200113066.  The employee

concrete floor.  Employee #1 sustained blunt force traumatic injuries and was

At 1:30 p.m. on October 5, 2020, Employees #1, #2, and #3, employed by a precast
concrete and structural steel company, were installing precast concrete stairs
for a new 15-story commercial building, a multi-employer construction project.
They were on the 13th and 14th floors and adjusting the stairs for proper
elevation.  The employees were using a 20-foot webbed sling and two 3-ton chain
hoists.  The stairs below the 13th floor had been installed, including necessary
welding.  The stairs on the 13th and 14th floors were not yet welded or secured.
The employees were in the process of adjusting the stairs for proper elevation
when the 14th floor staircase collapsed and hit the 13th floor.  This caused all
of the stairs directly below to collapse as well.  The three employees, who were
tied off to the staircases, were pulled down with the collapsing concrete, which
had a total weight of approximately 75,000 pounds.  The employees and concrete
fell down the staircase shaft, a fall height of approximately 150 feet.
Employees #1, #2, and #3 were all killed.
At 7:10 a.m. on October 5, 2020, an employee was clearing the film from the
heating plate on the Maxwell Chase Double Tray Sealer, when the blade came down.
The employee's fingers were caught in the machine. The employee's left index
finger was amputated.  The employee was hospitalized.

operator on Chop Saw #2. The outfeed conveyor of the chop saw automatically shut

hydraulics to the star kicker from the control cab of the chop saw which left
the star kicker in a down position just over the chain conveyor. The employee
failed to lock out the chain conveyor and proceeded to walk out on to the chain
conveyor to clear debris from the photo eye. Employee #1's right foot was on the
chain conveyor and as the photo eye was cleared, the conveyor belt began moving,
drawing his right foot and lower leg between the conveyor and star kicker dog.
The employee suffered a large abrasion to his right calf, closed fractures of
his right medial and lateral malleolus with a tibiotalar dislocation, and damage
to several nerves and tendons. The employee was hospitalized for treatment.
At 3:15 p.m. on September 17, 2020, Employee #1, a framing contractor working on
a concrete tilt-up building, was installing 2"x8" roof joists. The joists were
set in hangers secured to the roof structure on one side and resting unsecured
on a steel ledger on the other side. After returning from break and preparing to
resume work, Employee #1 tripped near the opening on the roof, causing his foot
to land on a joist hanger. The unsecured joist slid off the steel bar, and
despite attempting to grasp a nearby joist to control his fall, the joist gave
way, and he fell approximately 14 feet to the ground. Employee #1 sustained a
leg fracture. At the time of the fall, Employee #1 had not yet donned the
required fall protection (PFAS) for the task.  The employee was hospitalized for
treatment.
At 3:50 p.m. on October 5, 2020, Employee #1, employed by a site preparation
company, was operating a 637E Cat Scraper Series II The Scraper to clear ground
for a new project.  The equipment rolled over the top edge of a hill and down
the slope.  During the roll-over, Employee #1, who was not using a seat belt,
was ejected.  The Scraper struck and rolled over Employee #1, who was fatally
crushed.
At 12:45 p.m. on September 21, 2020, an employee and his coworkers were
harvesting sweet potatoes in one of the employer's fields. They were performing
normal work duties sorting sweet potatoes into bins on the harvester. The
temperature was between 90 and 93 degrees.  At noon they took a 30-minute lunch

At 8:30 a.m. on July 31, 2020, Employee #1 was working for a structural

At 8:00 a.m. on March 29, 2020, an employee worked as housekeeper and last

At 9:45 a.m. on June 23, 2020, Employee # 1 was cleaning a rental property. She

At 1:30 p.m. on September 1, 2020, an employee was working as a machine operator
for a firm that made aerospace and industrial equipment. He was operating an EPG
pneumatic bearing press on the firm's operations floor. This was not his usual
workstation. He had been trained on this machine, but he was not aware that an
unauthorized modification made to it to address operational issues had created a
hazard. Before the modification, tooling would turn in during stator spacer
pressing, a routine job. The modification prevented the tooling from turning in.
During the machine's modification, a torque restraint bar blocking plate had
been attached to the machine's ram cylinder. The modification had created a
crushed-by hazard and amputation hazard for employees. When the ram cylinder
raised after being activated by the machine's two-hand controls, a pinch point
was created. This pinch point was not fully guarded during the machine's entire
operating cycle, particularly during the upswing of the ram cylinder. All the
firm's machine operators were required to know how to operate at least two
different types of machines to be fully qualified for their jobs. A machine
operator who was more familiar with this press was absent on the day of
incident, and the employee, unaware of the pinch point, was taking his place.
The employee pressed and released the two-hand activation buttons and then
turned to speak with a coworker. There was a pause between cycles, and in that
time, the employee inadvertently put his hand above the torque restraint bar
blocking plate, the attachment added during the modification. When the pneumatic
operating system released the ram cylinder, the cylinder rose. The tips of the
index and middle fingers on the employee's right hand were crushed between the
torque restraint bar blocking plate and the base of the ram cylinder. The extent
of the injuries necessitated the surgical partial amputation of the two fingers.
The employee was hospitalized.

the coil tipped over and pinned the employee to a guardrail. A coworker freed
the employee from the guardrail and the employer's EMS service attempted to
resuscitate the employee. The employee died, on site, from his injuries.
An employee was working as a project estimator for a firm that manufactured
sheet metal products. It specialized in stainless steel fabrication and
equipment production. He contracted COVID-19, becoming symptomatic in mid-July
2020. He was hospitalized for several weeks, before he died on August 22, 2020.
The death was attributed to complications associated with infection with
COVID-19. Contact tracing conducted by the employer determined that it was
possible that work-related exposure contributed to the employee's contraction of
COVID-19.
At 3:55 p.m. on March 4, 2020, Employee #1 was on a roof not wearing fall
protection while a coworker operated a forklift to stock the roof with materials
(plywood). As the coworker placed the plywood on the roof joists, the plywood
moved causing Employee #1 to fall 13 feet to a lower level.  Employee #1
suffered lacerations to his leg, bruises, and a fractured shoulder and was
hospitalized.
At 10:30 a.m. on August 14, 2020, Employee #1, employed by a painting company,
was engaged in repainting the exterior of a residential structure.  He was
working from a ladder and hanging plastic in preparation for painting when the
ladder slipped.  Employee #1 fell, a fall height of 16 feet, and struck the
concrete surface.  He sustained blunt force traumatic injuries, including
multiple fractures, and was killed.
At 7:50 a.m. on August 25, 2020, an employee was riding on the back of a trash
truck doing trash collections. The employee fell off the back of the truck and
struck his head on a curb. The employee was killed.
At 1:45 p.m. on August 21, 2020, Employee #1 climbed a ladder to the perlite
mixer on the Deralite line. Employee #1 fell 9.5 feet off of the Perlite mixer
catwalk, when the lid of the mixer he was using for stability came loose.
Employee #1 sustained lacerations to his head and received 12 staples. Employee
#1 was hospitalized.
At 12:00 a.m. on August 25, 2020, an employee was cleaning out concrete mixture
from the feeder.  The employee crushed his hand/wrist moving a plate in the
feeder.  The employee was hospitalized.
At 5:00 p.m. on July 19, 2020, an employee started a tabber assembly machine to
ensure that it was operating within a preset parameter as part of a
troubleshooting  process. The employee bypassed a door panel safety sensor in
order to expedite visual inspection. With one of the panel doors open, the
employee attempted to adjust a wire base by placing his right hand underneath
it. The wire base came down on his hand and partially amputated his middle
finger, requiring hospitalization.
At 1:00 p.m. on August 20, 2020, Employee #1 was cleaning the concrete chute of
the concrete truck, when a coworker arrived to clean the bucket of the track
hoe.  The brake of the track hoe was enabled when Employee #1 parked and left
the equipment.  The coworker's lunch box reportedly fell on to the bucket
controls, and the bucket swung and struck Employee #1, who was standing between
the concrete truck and the track hoe. Employee #1 was struck in the upper
abdomen by the bucket of the track hoe.  The employee sustained blunt force
trauma and was hospitalized for treatment.
At 10:15 a.m. on August 18, 2020, an employee was clearing a jammed tote on an
assembly conveyor when he grabbed the conveyor belt and it began to move. When
the belt moved, the employee caught his fingers in the nip point of the
conveyor. The employee was hospitalized to treat amputation of two fingers.
At 1:45 p.m. on August 20, 2020, an employee was inspecting brushes on a
generator. The employee's left thumb was struck by and cut by the rotating fan.
The employee was treated without hospitalization.
An employee was working at a nursing care or skilled nursing facility. The
employer's human resources office stated that the employee was not a regular
employee and that her last day of work was March 14, 2020. The employee was not
working at the time she was thought to have contracted COVID-19. Instead, she
was visiting and taking care of her father in a convalescent home. On May 1,
2020, she was diagnosed with COVID-19. She was hospitalized from May 1, 2020,
thru May 16, 2020. The company was informed that she had died on May 16, 2020.
The firm did not consider the death a job-related fatality. According to the
firm's facility administrator, the facility did not have a resident with a
confirmed case of COVID-19 until April 8, 2020. Over the next six weeks, 32
residents and eight staff employee members out of 99 employees in the facility
were diagnosed as COVID-19-positive. Only people in the the East and North Wings
were affected. There were six resident deaths and no employee deaths. After
this, according to the Center for Medicare Services (CMS) report, the next time
a resident diagnosed positive for COVID-19 was on August 2, 2020.
At 4:00 p.m. on August 19, 2020, an employee was operating a bandsaw, cutting
metal piping.  The employee reached into the pipe while the blade was cutting
through the pipe.  The employee suffered a fingertip amputation to the left
middle finger and was treated without hospitalization.
At 9:30 a.m. on June 25, 2020, an employee working as an operating engineer
working for a winery was pruning vines with tractor fitted with a Clemens EL50
Leaf Remover attachment. The employee had been operating the tractor trimming
the vineyard moving down the vineyard rows when he noticed that the attachment
became jammed. The employee attempted to clear the jam with the machine still
running. When the employee cleared the debris from the rollers, his fingers were
pinched by the rollers and crushed. A coworker noticed that the employee had
stopped and was raising his left hand in the air. The coworker proceeded to help
free the employee's fingers from the attachment. The employee was transported to
the hospital, where he was hospitalized to treat a crushing injury to his right
hand.
An employee was working in the automation area of a meat processing facility.
The employee tested positive for COVID-19 on June 10, 2020, and was admitted to
the hospital on June 15, 2020. The employee was placed on a ventilator on June
23, 2020 and subsequently died on July 2, 2020.
At 8:00 p.m. on July 9, 2020, an employee who had worked as a Steam-Vac Operator
on the "Kill Floor" of an animal slaugtering plant died from COVID-19. On April
28, 2020, the Employee was tested for COVID-19 and reported positive on May 1,
2020. The employee's last work day was on April 30, 2020. The date, time and
other details leading up to exposure are not indicated in the narrative but the
employer did not have an adequate respiratory protection program in place.
At 11:15 a.m. on August 15, 2020, an employee working as a construction laborer
for a commercial building contractor was installing drywall. The employee was
using an A-frame ladder in the closed position on top of a rolling scaffold when
he fell to the concrete floor below. The employee was hospitalized to treat
At 3:30 a.m. on September 2, 2020, an employee was assisting the bread machine
operator clear a jam on the blade area. The employee put his left hand in the
unguarded area. The employee lacerated his left middle finger. The employee went
to the hospital for surgery but was not hospitalized.
An employee was working as a travelling radiology technician at a large teaching
hospital taking chest X-rays of COVID-19 patients multiple times each day. The
employee was provided with PPE by the hospital. The employee contracted COVID-19
and became ill so she did not work her planned shifts on August 14 and 15. On
August 16, 2020, the employee was hospitalized with COVID-19. The employee's
condition deteriorated, and she died on September 02, 2020.
At 12:00 p.m. on October 10, 2020, an employee worked as a meat seller in a meat
market. On October 10, 2020, the employee died due to COVID-19-related illness.
An employee was working as a clinical nurse in the adult acute and intermediate
medicine department of a medical center. The employee was providing patient care
to individuals infected with COVID-19. It was determined that the employer's
aerosol transmissible disease program was ineffective and there was inadequately
investigation of COVID-19 exposure incidents. The employee was hospitalized at
8:00 a.m. on September 25, 2020, in the medical center where she worked, for
symptoms associated with COVID-19 infection.
At 6:20 a.m. on August 6, 2020, Employee #1 was removing the guard over the top
sheave of an elevator when he inadvertently hit the down button with his right
hand. This action caused his left forearm to be drawn into the mechanism,
resulting in a broken wrist. Employee #1 was hospitalized for treatment.
At 2:00 p.m. on August 24, 2020, Employee #1 was inside the scaffold drilling
the plywood panels into the insulated forming blocks of the southeast corner
wall. Employee #1 was standing inside the 9-foot scaffold, fainted, and fell.
Employee #1 sustained the following injuries: scalp laceration, scalp hematoma,
closed fracture of multiple ribs of both sides, syncope and T10 vertebral
fracture. Employee #1 was hospitalized.  Employee #1 was injured due to exposure
to direct sunlight and a high temperature of 108 degrees Fahrenheit, and the
lack of a break.
An employee was working as a housekeeper in a skilled nursing facility that
included an in-patient rehabilitation and medical treatment center staffed with
trained medical professionals. On April 20, 2020, the employee was transported
to a regional medical center and hospitalized for the treatment of COVID-19.
At 12:45 p.m. on October 15, 2020, an employee sustained an amputation of the
thumb while attempting to remove a knot from polyester webbing, as the webbing
was pulled by a dye range machine.  The employee was treated without
hospitalization.
At 7:30 a.m. on October 15, 2020, Employee #1, a field service technician, had
used a forklift truck to load a drive unit into a van. Employee #1 exited the
forklift in order to straighten up the unit in the van. While doing so, the
forklift rolled forward, pinning Employee #1 between the bumper of the van and
the forklift. Employee #1 was hospitalized to treat broken bones in the right
leg.
At 11:42 a.m. on August 25, 2020, Employee #1 removed a sanitary manhole cover
to determine whether the confined space had any water accumulation. Employee #1
then entered the manhole and was followed by Employees #2 and #3. A nearby
coworker noticed the employees entering the space and at some point went over to
see how they were doing. The coworker found Employees #2 and #3 trying to revive
Employee #1. The coworker went to call emergency services and upon return to the
manhole, the coworker could no longer hear any sounds from the employees in the
space. All three employees were killed due to low oxygen levels in the space
(measured at 5%).
At 11:00 a.m. on October 16, 2020, Employee #1 was adjusting a suspended load on
a forklift when the temporary wood guardrail he was leaning on broke. The
employee fell approximately 38 feet to the lower concrete level. Emergency
responders transported the employee by ambulance, and he was hospitalized and
underwent facial reconstruction surgery and treatment for internal bleeding. The
incident highlights the need for ensuring the structural integrity of temporary
guardrails and the importance of fall protection measures in construction
environments.
On October 21, 2020, a 20-year-old employee was working for a drywall and
insulation contractor. His employer was doing interior work at a one-story
single-family home. The employee was removing existing insulation from the attic
above the garage, when he saw a snake beneath the insulation. Startled by the
snake, and attempting to exit the attic, he stepped backward off the planks
supporting him. He fell through the drywall of the ceiling approximately 10 feet
(3.0 m) to the cement floor of the garage. He suffered an abrasion to his head.
He was treated without hospitalization. The foreman had allowed employees to
work on a walking/working surface with areas that did not have the strength and
structural integrity to support an employee's weight. Areas between rafters
where insulation was installed on top of drywall ceiling were not capable of
supporting an employee's weight. No fall protection system was in use to prevent
an employee from falling through the drywall ceiling.
At 1:15 p.m. on October 20, 2020, an employee was working as a brick mason and
stonemason for a waterproofing service. The firm was installing HVAC and
associated equipment on the flat roof of a commercial building. This was a
maintenance or repair project. A crew of four workers was moving a swing stage
scaffold from an upper roof to a lower roof section. Two workers were on the
upper section and two were on the lower section. The two workers on the lower
section were the employee and one of his coworkers. They were carrying a support
beam for the swing stage scaffold, with one worker on each end of the beam. The
beam was 24 feet (7.3-meters) long. The workers were walking backward. The
employee and his coworker were working about 17 feet (5.2 m) away from the edge
of the roof. The coworker stopped walking, because he thought they were where
they needed to be. The employee, who was the nearer of the two to the edge of
the roof, continued to walk backward. He fell through an open roof hatch used to
access the roof. He fell 17 feet (5.2 m) and suffered head injuries when he
landed on the floor. He was hospitalized. The employees were not using personal
fall arrest systems. No guardrails were erected between the employees and the
edge of the roof. The hole created by the roof access was not covered, and no
guard rails had been erected around its opening. No safety nets were installed.
The employer did not ensure that the employees were protected from falling
through the roof hatch by personal fall arrest systems, covers, or guardrail
systems. The foreman was on the roof line above the injured employee. He was
directing the activities involving the movement of the swing stage scaffold. He
was in a position to see the hazard, but he did not take the necessary steps to
abate or minimize the hazard. The roof hatch was equipped with an alarm.
According to the security logs the hatch had been open since approximately 9:00
a.m.
At 12:00 p.m. on September 10, 2024, Employee #1 was attempting to wire a well
pump when the employee used wire strippers to remove sheathing from wires in
preparation for a voltage test. The wire strippers made contact with live
conductors, causing an electrical shock. The shock caused the employee to fall
to the ground onto their chest and prevented the employee from breaking the
electrical pathway. The 220V circuit eventually tripped the breaker, allowing
the employee to call for help. The employee was transported to the hospital and
admitted for treatment of the electrical shock.
At 6:30 p.m. on October 21, 2020, an employee was operating a powered industrial
truck. The employee was struck by another powered industrial truck and sustained
an amputation of his foot, resulting in hospitalization.
At 6:30 a.m. on October 21, 2020, an employee was was straightening a panel
above an auger. His right leg became caught in auger and was amputated above the
knee. He was hospitalized.
At 1:00 p.m. on October 20, 2020, an employee was operating a seamer machine.
When the machine jammed, she attempted to clear the machine by reaching into the
area of operation.  The employee lacerated her right index finger and was
hospitalized.
At 12:00 p.m. on October 16, 2020, Employee #1 was attempting to remove bracket
scaffolding from the side of a building.  He fell approximately 20 feet to the
ground. The Division was notified on October 16, 2020, and arrived on the scene
on October 22, 2020. The Division spoke with the onsite foreman, who reported
that there were no witnesses to the fall. It was unclear whether the employee
fell from the bracket scaffold or the roof. The foreman stated that a bracket
and two scaffold planks were found on the ground near the injured employee. The
employee was wearing a harness at the time of the accident, but it was not
connected to a lanyard. The employee sustained a broken vertebra, broken
shoulder, broken ribs, a punctured lung, hip damage, concussion, and memory
loss. He was transported to St. Louise Hospital and later transferred to Valley
Medical Center in San Jose, CA for admission and treatment.
At 1:30 p.m. on April 28, 2020, Employee #1, employed by a construction company,
was working at a multiemployer project, the construction of a residential
structure.  He jumped into a trench and made contact with a shovel handle
almonds.  The employee stuck his foot under the landing gear of the truck and
