At 9:30 a.m. on August 26, 2020, Employee #1, employed by an electrical services
company, was working at a medical center.  He was on a stepladder and removing
fluorescent lighting fixtures in preparation for installing LED lighting
fixtures.  The employee had not been properly trained in hazardous electrical
work, and power to the fixtures had not been turned off.  Employee #1
experienced an electric shock which burned his fingers.  He fell from the ladder
and struck his head on the floor.  The employee was killed.
At 11:00 a.m. on August 28, 2020, an employee was shredding cabbage with a food
processing machine (Robot Coupe CL 50). The employee was hand-feeding cabbage
into the food processing machine.  The employee reached too far into the
machine, and the tips of her right index and middle fingers contacted the
rotating blade (point of operation) of the machine, causing amputation injuries.
The employee was hospitalized.
At 9:45 a.m. on October 6, 2020, Employee #1 was working for a structural
steel/concrete contractor. Employee #1 was removing metal roofing. Employee #1
climbed out of a scissor lift and onto the roof and he fell 16 feet through a
skylight.  Employee #1 suffered a fractured hip along with trauma to the face
and head.  Employee #1 was hospitalized.
An employee was working as a production cook at a general medical and surgical
hospital. He was hospitalized for COVID-19. He began experiencing symptoms of
and tested positive for COVID-19 on September 16, 2020. He was hospitalized on
September 20, 2020. At approximately 7:30 p.m. on October 11, 2020, he died from
COVID-19 at the hospital where he was employed. His employer informed OSHA of
the death via a serious event report at 2:10 p.m. on October 13, 2020, and a
call to the OSHA hotline at 4:11 p.m., also on October 13, 2020. The employer's
human resources director said that she first became aware of the fatality on
Monday, October 12, 2020, at the morning meeting when, the food service director
had asked for prayers for a long-term employee who had died. The OSHA inspector
did not recommend a violation for late reporting of a fatality, since the
employee had died 31 days after the determined possible exposure date of
September 10, 2020. A violation for late reporting of a hospitalization was
similarly not recommended, since the employee had been hospitalized on September
20, 2020 or ten days after the exposure date. Coworkers who were interviewed
stated that the employee had never missed a day of work. The food service
director said that she had worked with the employee on Tuesday, September 15,
2020, and he was fine. She said he called her on Wednesday, September 16, 2020,
and said he was not feeling well. He hoped it was just his sinuses, and he said
that he was going to get tested.
Employee #1 was a melter who put metal into an oven foundry area. Employee #2
was a machinist in the back machine shop, and primarily operated a lathe. Other
employees had symptoms of COVID-19 and a total of 15 employees tested positive
between August 25, and September 2, 2020. Employee #1 felt the onset of symptoms
on August 27, and was sent to be tested for COVID-19. Employee #1 tested
positive and was hospitalized with COVID-19 from September 2-7, 2020. When
Employee #1 was hospitalized, the employer shut down the facility for two weeks
while employees were tested, quarantined, and isolated.  Employee #2 began
having symptoms of COVID-19 on August 25, and his last day at the facility was
August 27. Employee #2 was hospitalized on September 1, 2020, and had been
intubated. Employee #2 died on October 12, 2020.
At 8:45 p.m. on October 5, 2020, an employee was cleaning the tube pucks and
jaws of the Kalix KX800 tube filling machine. The employee's finger was pinched
in the machine, resulting in an avulsion of the fingertip.  The employee was
hospitalized.
On September 17, 2020, an employee working for a tree removal company was
feeding branches into a Bandit Model 250XP trailer type brush chipper. The
employee was feeding an approximately 6-foot by 4-inch branch into the chipper.
The branch had a bend that caught the employee by the hip and pulled her into
the chipper. The employee lacerated to both legs and her pelvic region. The
employee sustained severe trauma on the right knee requiring surgical amputation
of the leg above the knee. The employee was hospitalized for 14 days.
At 10:15 a.m. on September 24, 2020, an employee was operating a Rocheleau blow
molder.  The employee was monitoring the movement of the plastic bottles coming
out of the mold tunnel.  He observed that a bottle had come out of the cradle
and was stuck in the molding chamber. Instead of opening/sliding the interlock
guarding system/safety door, he put his left hand through the bottle cradle
opening and grabbed the stuck bottle from the molding chamber. As a result, his
left index and middle finger made contact with the edge of the mold unit, which
was in the compressing/moving mode.  He sustained a partial amputation of the
left index and middle finger.  The employee was admitted and discharged from
Highland Hospital within 14 hours. The employee did not follow lockout/tagout
procedures, and there was inadequate guarding.
At 10:45 p.m. on September 11, 2020, an employee working as a machine operator
for a motor vehicle parts manufacturer was adjusting a jammed metal tube (stock)
so that it would continue to feed into the cutting machine. Upon dislodging the
tube, the employee caught his left-hand pinky finger between the tube and the
guide. The employee amputated his finger requiring hospitalization.
At 10:15 a.m. on October 12, 2020, an employee working for a company that leases
industrial machinery was performing maintenance on a forklift. The employee was
adjusting the chain for clearance when the mast fell and struck his sheared his
right ring finger. The employee amputated his ring finger and partially
amputated his pinky finger which was reattached. The employee received medical
treatment but not hospitalization.
On October 6, 2020, Employee #1, employed by a construction company, was working
at a multi-employer construction project for a new residential structure.  He
was using a SkyTrak Rough Terrain Forklift with a homemade platform basket and
installing exterior siding.  The platform basket had no side rails, and the
employee was not using a personal fall arrest system.  The employee walked
backward on the platform and fell from the unguarded right side, a fall height
of 17 feet.  He hit his head on a concrete patio.  Emergency services
transported the employee to the hospital, where he died of fall-related injuries
two weeks later.
At 9:55 a.m. on October 12, 2020, an employee was moving the server rack from
the testing room to the Packing Room. The employee was injured when the server
rack weighing approximately 1,700 pounds tipped over on top of him, crushing his
right leg. The employee was transported to the hospital for treatment.
At approximately 10:15 a.m. on April 16, 2020, an employee, working for a
construction and septic contractor, was operating a drill rig. The employee
exited the rig, removed an unsecured cover, and fell into an open 35 feet deep
by 3 feet wide hole. The employee was hospitalized and treated for broken ribs,
sternum, vertebrae, left foot, and ankle.
At 5:43 p.m. on June 19, 2020, an employee was operating a waverunner as part of
a guided tour.  The waverunner became stalled, and he jumped into the water to
unclog it . The employee was killed after he drowned while wearing a life vest.
At 10:15 a.m. on October 12, 2020, an employee working as a foreman for a tree
service was working at a rural site located at GPS coordinates 38.497504,
contact with a COVID-19-positive patient. The employee had exposure to his
coworkers. He contracted COVID-19.  On April 8, 2020, he died.
On September 2, 2020, an employee who had been working as anesthesiologist at an
ambulatory surgical center died of COVID-19. The center performed surgical
procedures only on patients who were tested and confirmed to be COVID-19
negative. The employee was tested and diagnosed with COVID-19. Prior to the
employee's illness, none of his coworkers exhibited any COVID-19 related
symptoms or had been found to be COVID-19 positive. The employer did not receive
any notices of patients testing positive for COVID-19 post surgical procedure.
The employee did not perform any emergency procedures. Information regarding
engineering, administrative and personal protective equipment controls for
COVID-19 are not included in the narrative.
At 10:00 p.m. on May 20, 2020, Employee #1 was working for an insulation
contractor.  Employee #1 was walking on the scaffold resulting a fall.  Employee
#1 was hospitalized to treat unspecified injuries.

plugged shot transfer conveyor on a Jet Wheel Blast Shot Blast Machine when he
told Coworker #1 to wait for day shift maintenance to repair the machine. The
employee instructed Coworker #1 to dump the parts from the machine into a second
machine, which Coworker #1 did as instructed. Coworker #1 left the machine
without shutting it down. Approximately 10 - 15 minutes later, Coworker #1
returned to the machine to finish the shutdown process and did not see the

position crushing the employee between the rotating member of the shot blast

At 9;30 a.m. on September 23, 2020, an employee was working for a firm that made
envelopes. He was a machine operator. He was on the facility's work floor green.
He was operating work floor green's Winkler + D�nnebier model 627 RC envelope
production machine, with serial number15.982. He was setting it up for use. He
was watching paper as it was fed through the machine. The paper that was being
fed jammed in the machine. The employee reached into the machine while it was
running at production speed to pull out the jammed paper. His fingers were
pulled into the bottom flap-folding section of the machine. They came into
contact with the revolving blade in that section. The tips of the employee's
right middle finger and right thumb were amputated. The employee was treated
without hospitalization. The guards had been removed from the machine in that
the safety interlock that would have allowed the machine to run in "inching
mode" had been disabled. This condition was noted, apparently during an
inspection, on or about October 5, 2020. At the same time, it was noted that the
employer had not ensured that the employee had been given authorized employee
training. This condition exposed employees conducting service or maintenance to
amputation hazards.  Finally, it was also noted at that time that the employer
had not ensured that employee lock out/tagout training had been administered and
records kept of that training.
At 4:55 p.m. on September 26, 2020, Employee #1, employed by a solar panel
installation company, was replacing a bad connector on a solar panel wiring
harness. Employee #2 mistakenly plugged in the wrong wiring harness and
attempted to pull it apart, causing an arc flash that burned the end of the
cable. As Employee #2 went to cut the end off to replace it, they sustained a
shock when Employee #1 was cutting through the second wire. The employee's elbow
touched a metal framing, causing them to become grounded and shocked. The shock
resulted in an irregular heart rate. The employee was treated for the injury but
did not require hospitalization.
At 11:10 a.m. on June 30, 2020, Employee #1 was removing and replacing a roof on
a residential structure without using any fall protection. Employee #1 working
with a coworker, removed the entire roof including the plywood sheathing.
Employee #1 fell through the open roof trusses and through the bedroom ceiling
below. Employee #1 was hospitalized to treat injuries to his back and right knee
and underwent surgery.  The employee was hospitalized.
At 4:30 a.m. on October 2, 2020, an employee working as a fire fighter for a
correctional institution was mopping up after a fire damaged a tree. He
sustained head and spinal injuries when the tree fell on the employee. The
employee was hospitalized to treat a concussion and multiple contusions and
abrasions.
At 12:00 p.m. on March 30, 2020, Employee # 1 was cutting a tree down. The tree
fell over and kicked backwards horizontally. The tree branches struck Employee #
1 in the back and head. He was killed.
At 7:45 a.m. on September 28, 2020, an employee was operating a fuel cell. The
employee's finger became caught in a pneumatic cylinder end and the wall. The
employee's right middle finger pad was amputated. The employee was treated
without hospitalization.
At 1:00 a.m. on March 19, 2020, an employee was working at a scrap metal
recycling rail yard.  Prior to the incident occurring, the employee was
accomplishing normal rail yard procedures and preparing to couple a rail car and
rail engine, so that it could be transported to one of the recycling warehouses.
The rail car was stationary, and the rail engine was being operated by the
"operator." Just as the operator and his rail engine approached the rail car,
the employee turned away to reach for a snatch block, which is a block of wood
used to stop a rail car from moving in the event it is needed.  When the
employee turned around and the rail car and engine were in view, he realized
that the couplers were not aligned properly and ran into the area between the
cars, while the engine was moving, and used his right leg and foot to try to
align the couplers.  His right foot was caught in and crushed between the
couplers.  After emergency response and transport to the emergency room at
Barnes Jewish hospital, the employee's toes were amputated.  His condition
worsened overnight and his lower leg, below the knee, was amputated the next
day.  The employee was hospitalized.  The operator was not injured.
At 11:45 a.m. on September 29, 2020, Employee #1, employed by a construction
company, was engaged in a demolition project.  He was cutting a vertical
concrete wall when the wall collapsed onto the employee.  Employee #1 was
killed.
At 9:30 a.m. on October 1, 2020, an employee was working for a farm merchant
wholesaler and was inside a grain bin. The bin auger and sweeper energized at
the time. While in the bin, the employee contacted the auger with his right leg.
The employee was hospitalized to treat an amputation to his leg below the knee.
An employee was working as a certified nurse assistant in a skilled nursing

At 2:30 p.m. on July 30, 2020, while at the Cracker Breaker, an employee was

At 10:40 a.m. on July 10, 2020, an employee working for a state department of

The employee was hospitalized to treat a broken right shoulder and four broken
ribs.
At 6:30 p.m. on May 20, 2020, an employee was removing paper that got stuck
coming out of the wicket UV dryer on a printing press. The employee's finger was

At approximately 3:30 p.m. on April 13, 2020, an employee contracted COVID-19

At 7:30 a.m. on July 20, 2020, an employee prepared to install a cable railing

At 8:30 a.m. on February 15, 2020, Employee # 1, employed by a construction

The paper that was placed on the roof before the shingles are installed has an

Employee #1 was hospitalized for treatment.
At 1:15 p.m. on July 2, 2020, an employee climbed onto of a dumpster and was
arranging boxes and wood to make more room. At some point, the employee fell

the excavator causing the boom to swing striking Employee #1.  Employee #1
suffered fractured ribs and was hospitalized.
At 1:30 p.m. on July 23, 2020, an employee became infected with COVID-19 and
died.
At 8:13 on July 17, 2020, an employee was working alone adjusting the stop on a
86 Ton Metal Muncher Hydraulic Multi-Station Ironworker Model MM90C preparing

The machine cycled and caught the employee's finger between the frame and the

At 9:00 a.m. on July 27, 2020, an employee was mowing grass with a Toro
Groundsmaster 4000D mower along a highway. A the employee was mowing he

of the mower. The employee attempted to regain control but the mower rolled down
the slope coming to rest approximately 24 feet from where the rollover
initiated. The employee was hospitalized to treat multiple lacerations and rib
fractures.
At noon on August 4, 2020, an employee was working for a landscaping service. He
was getting into a truck after picking up litter in the median of an interstate
highway. As he was rounding the front of the truck to get inside, the driver of
a passing pickup truck veered off the highway and struck the employee. The
employee suffered multiple fractures and internal traumatic injuries. He was
killed.
At approximately 6:20 a.m. on Wednesday, August 5, 2020, an employee was working
for an intermodal freight transport company or trucking carrier. He picked up
and drove semi-trailer truck number P9032 into the firm's yard. He located
shipping container number BMOU3075767. He backed his truck into the chassis and
secured it to the fifth wheel mechanism, located at the rear of the truck. He
stepped out of the truck cabin to attach the red and blue air lines to the
chassis along with the electric cable. Once these were securely connected, the
employee walked around the truck to get access to the crank of the landing gear
legs. Either he did not apply the brakes, or the brakes were ineffective. As the
landing gear legs retracted up off the ground, the truck and chassis rolled
backward and sideways toward the employee. The employee was caught in between
the moving chassis container and another stationary container located behind
him. He was ultimately pinned between these two containers. A coworker, who was
working nearby, discovered the employee pinned between the two containers and
immediately entered the cabin of truck number P9032. The coworker applied both
the trailer air supply brakes and the parking brakes. The employee was crushed
between two shipping containers and was killed. He was immediately pronounced
dead on the scene. DOSH learned of this event on Wednesday, August 5, 2020, from
an officer of the Los Angeles Port Police, who reported this incident to the
Cal/OSHA Long Beach district office. On the same day, the Division held an
opening conference with the employer at 9:30 a.m.
At 11:00 a.m. on August 2, 2020, an employee was caring for two patients in the
patient's home. The employee was scheduled to return to work on July 25, 2020,
but she informed her employer she was having COVID-19 symptoms.  The employee
went to the hospital the night of July 25, 2020 and received a COVID-19 test.
The employee was released from the hospital the same day.  The employee's test
returned positive and the employee did not return to work. The two patients, the

August 3, 2020, the father of the employee called the employer to inform them

At 11:30 p.m. on April 23, 2020, an employee performing job duties as a
Registered Nurse was exposed to COVID-19 and later died.
At 08:12 a.m. on July 14, 2020, an employee was cutting fabric on a machine. The

cutter blade, amputating the employee's right thumb tip. The employee was
treated but not hospitalized.
At 8:30 a.m. on April 30, 2020, an employee was working as a case dock laborer
and started feeling ill and went home. On April 3, 2020, the employee was
hospitalized and later died  on April 30, 2020 as a result of COVID-19. The
employee tested positive for COVID-19. No other employee at this time had tested
positive for COVID-19. The employee contracted the virus from another family
member in the household. Therefore, the employee's death was not occupational
related.
At 3:30 p.m. on August 4, 2020, Employees #1, #2, and #3, employed by a masonry
construction company, were working at a multi-employer construction project, a
new 18-story commercial building.  They were working from a fabricated welded
frame scaffold system with caster wheels and platform extension and installing
the brown coat mixture of Exterior Insulation and Finish System (EIFS) and
Portland Cement to the soffit with mesh embedded into the west base coat.  The

the roof, a fall height of approximately 30 feet.  The owner sustained blunt
force traumatic injuries and was killed.
At 8:00 a.m. on June 1, 2020, an employee was doing paperwork at a computer. The
employee was later tested positive for COVID-19. The employee later died.
At 11:26 a.m. on February 6, 2020, an employee and three coworkers were pruning
two madrone trees next to a building at a remote site. Two coworkers were
climbers that were each in one of the two trees using chain saws to trim
branches. The employee was removing the branches from below the trees while
another coworker was operating a chipper machine. The employee was walking under
the tree pulling a winch line from the chipper machine to a branch to be pulled
to the chipper. A coworker in the tree looked to see that the employee was not
below him in the drop zone then started making cuts in a branch but never looked
again to see if the drop zone remained clear before making the final cut and
dropping the branch. The tree branch was approximately 8 inches in diameter and
20 feet in length. The branch fell approximately 40 feet and struck the employee
who had walked into the drop zone. The crew was using verbal communications with
each other during the tree trimming operations including the grounds men yelling
up to the climber in the tree before entering the drop zone and the climber in
the tree yelling "headache" before cutting and dropping a branch. The employee
did not yell "headache" before finishing the final cut and dropping the branch.
The drop zones were not discussed before the trimming operations began as the
crew believed it was a "common knowledge" thing that the area below the employee
in the tree is the drop zone.  A drop zone could be under one side of the tree
At 8:00 a.m. on August 14, 2020, an employee reported to his coworker

At 12:45 a.m. on July 22, 2020, an employee was working as a baker for a bagel

At 12:49 p.m. on July 8, 2020, an employee was climbing down from the cab of a

At 6:00 p.m. on July 16, 2020, Employee #1 and Employee #2 were working to

# 1 and #2 were working in the trash box when the trash box became unbalanced

At 2:59 p.m. on July 21, 2020, an employee was fatally struck by the Royal coil

traveling in the forward direction with a loaded coil, slightly raised
lacerations to his head and arms.
At 1:51 p.m. on February 29, 2020, Employee #1 was employed by a construction
general contractor. The jobsite was for construction of a carwash.  Employees
were working on excavating the dirt surrounding the foundation of the property
line retaining wall.  The excavator operator removed the wall bracing to begin
digging the dirt surrounding the foundation. Employee #1 was assisting in
removing excess dirt when the wall collapsed and fell on him.  Employee #1
fractured both legs and was hospitalized.
At 1:24 p.m. on August 21, 2020, an employee was cleaning, picking up trash and
taking pictures of containers before set for shipment. A Coworker #1 observed
that the employee did not appear to be well and informed the employee to take a
break, drink water, and go to the breakroom to inform a Coworker #2
(supervisor). The employee informed the Coworker #2 that it was too hot and he
was leaving early. The employee collapsed after arriving home and died.
At 1:00 p.m. on March 4, 2020, Employee #1 retrieved his forklift from the

were retrained after the accident.  The employee's finger was fractured when
caught in between the forklifts during the collision.  The employee was
hospitalized.
At 10:50 a.m. on August 24, 2020, Employee #1 and a coworker, employed by a

an excavation while Coworker #2 operated an excavator to dig a basement for a

Coworker #2, not seeing the employee , began to operate the excavator to
continue digging in the excavation. The excavator bucket struck the employee,
tore the employee in half, and killed him.
At 11:32 a.m. on July 21, 2020, an employee was working on a pump jack
scaffolding system without fall protection. At some point, the employee fell

unspecified injuries.
Employee # 1 was working as a program instructor, providing care to residents.

negative coronavirus test. On or about August 5, 2020, she was placed on a
ventilator.  At 11:00 a.m. on August 9, 2020, she died. The death certificate
listed the cause of death as complications due to COVID-19.
At 9:15 a.m. on September 8, 2020, an employee was standing at the driver's side

dump truck outside the repair shop, with the truck in gear and the parking brake
turned off, so he and the excavation manager could adjust the slack adjusters on
each air brake. The coworker finished adjusting the slack adjusters and the

were preparing to start the truck in order to conduct a final test of the air
braking system. The employee was standing near the driver's side tandem axle
when the excavation manager opened the driver's side door and, while standing on
the ground, started the truck. The coworker, also standing at the driver's side
of the truck, yelled to the excavation manager too late that the truck was still
in gear. The truck lunged forward when the key was turned and the employee was
run over. The medical examiner pronounced the employee dead at the scene with
cause of death being a fractured skull with additional injuries to the chest,
torso, and leg.
At 2:00 p.m. on August 28, 2020, Employee #1 had just finished cleaning a dryer
vent located on the roof of a single-story residential home. To access the roof,
the employee used a fixed ladder on the work truck, then stepped from the truck
to the roof. After completing the work, the employee stepped off the roof onto
the truck and decided to change out the industrial vacuum bags housed inside the
truck, which are accessed through hinged doors on top. While on top of the
truck, the employee accidentally stepped inside one of the vacuum bag holes and
fell backward off the truck. The employee fell 8 feet to the ground and was
rendered unconscious. The employee sustained a concussion and cracked vertebrae
from the fall.  The employee was hospitalized for treatment.
At 3:00 p.m. on August 29, 2020, an employee was operating a punch press.  The
employee's finger was caught in the point of operation during a cycle.  The
employee amputated a finger and was treated without hospitalization.
At 11:45 a.m. on August 19, 2020, an employee was making approximately 17 cuts
of plywood, using a coworker's personal table saw brought in from home.  The

saw, the employee used both hands to control the plywood material.  While
cutting the plywood, the employee's hand slipped.  His left thumb made contact
with the energized blade, causing a laceration which required surgical repair.
The employee was hospitalized.

PMC machines #1 through #3 formed the buckets with heat. Excess plastic sheet,

utilized trim cutters or grinders to shred the waste material. PMC machine #2

At 11:00 a.m. on August 24, 2020, an employee, a lineman, was replacing an air
brake switch at a distribution circuit.  The employee suffered arc flash burns
to the face and was hospitalized.
At 8:45 a.m. on August 1, 2020, two employees were walking in the overhead
maintenance area above the production floor in order to install electrical lines
for a new piece of equipment. While the employees were walking to the exit, the
panels they were walking on collapsed. Each employee fell approximately 14 feet
to the concrete floor below. Both employees sustained a broken leg and other
minor injuries. One of the two employees was admitted for surgery and
hospitalized overnight.
At 8:45 a.m. on August 1, 2020, two employees were walking in the ceiling area
of a production floor to install electrical lines for new equipment when the
panel they were stepping on collapsed. Both employees fell approximately 14 feet
to the concrete floor, resulting in broken legs and other minor injuries. One
employee required surgery and was hospitalized overnight. The other employee was
treated without hospitalization. The incident highlights the risks associated
with working in ceiling areas and the importance of ensuring structural
integrity in work environments to prevent falls.

On or about September 11, 2020, Employee # 1 went to the hospital on his own
after work for COVID -19 symptoms.
An employee was working as a medication aide in a skilled nursing facility. The
employee was off-duty for a week when he started having symptoms of COVID-19.
The employee had tested negative for COVID-19 two days prior to taking off from
work. After a week off of work, the employee tested positive for COVID-19. The
employee's symptoms worsened and he was hospitalized and subsequently died on
August 26, 2020.
At 2:30 p.m. on May 7, 2020, Employee #1 was working for a commercial general
contractor.  Employee #1 was delivering cement to worksite when he had a panic
attack. Employee #1 received medical treatment but was not hospitalized.
On or about May 8, 2020, Employee #1, a food assembler, worked her last full
day. At about 5:00 p.m. on Sunday, May 10, 2020, Employee #1 was admitted to the
hospital and tested for COVID-19.  On Monday, May 11, 2020, a relative of
Employee #1 notified the employer that Employee #1 was admitted to the hospital,
tested for COVID-19 and was awaiting results. On Wednesday, May 13, 2020, the
employer received notification that the result of the test was positive. The
employer contacted Employee #1's relative on Thursday, May 14, 2020 around 8:05
a.m. and verified that Employee # 1 was positive for COVID-19. The
hospitalization was reported to the state OSHA on May 14, 2020.
At 6:30 a.m. on September 3, 2020, an employee was verifying the direction of
operation on a three-way actuated valve. The employee was testing the three-way
actuated valve assembly to be installed in production.  While testing the valve,
the employee rested his hand on the top of the valve and, unbeknownst to the
employee, two fingers inside the valve body assembly.  When the ball cycled, it
closed on the port where his fingers were and amputated the tips of his middle
and ring fingers on his left hand. The employee was hospitalized.
At 9:00 a.m. on July 27, 2020, an employee was working alone on a 125 psi
pressurized system when a component broke and hit him in the face. The employee
incurred a gash to his forehead and broken right eye socket, requiring
hospitalization.
On March 29, 2020, Employee # 1 was working as a dietary aide. He had an
exposure to the COVID-19 pathogen. He died on April 18, 2020 due to COVID-19.
At 11:30 a.m. on September 9, 2020, an employee working as an electrician for an
electrical contractor was troubleshooting an inoperative light relay. The
employee contacted a live 277-volt electrical component and received an
electrical shock. The employee was hospitalized to treat electrical burns to his
fingers.
At 12:35 p.m. on July 22, 2020, Employee #1 was driving a Taylor-Dunn "tug" with
a pallet on the front of the unit. Employee #1 took a corner too wide and struck
an end cap railing, pushing the wooden pallet into the left leg of Employee #1.
Employee #1 was admitted and treated at the hospital for a fractured femur
requiring surgery.
On or about May 7, 2020, Employee # 1 suffered an infection from the SARS-COV-2
Coronavirus. She was home on quarantine and died from a COVID-19 respiratory
infection.
At 10:30 p.m. on September 4, 2020, an employee was cleaning product from around
an auger. She stumbled and put her hand out to catch herself.  Her hand went
into the unguarded auger. The employee amputated her thumb to the first joint
and was hospitalized.
At 12:00 p.m. on September 10, 2020, an employee was acting as hose man on a
cement truck (Putzmeister) to pour concrete for a new bridge. At some point,
contact was made with a nearby 13.2-kilovolt power line and the employee
received an electrical shock. The employee was killed by electrocution.
At 2:30 p.m. on August 9, 2020, Employee #1 was working for an electrical
contractor.  Employee #1 was replacing a 7,200 volt underground electrical
utility line. Employee #1 connected the utility wire to the transformer while
the transformer was still energized.  Employee #1 suffered electrical shock and
burns.  Employee #1 was hospitalized.
At 8:00 a.m. on August 28, 2020, Employee # 1, a licensed practical nurse, was
assigned to take care of patients. He contracted COVID-19 from an unknown source

At 2:00 p.m. on August 7, 2020, an employee was operating a foot-operated press
when he went to retrieve a part and accidently pushed the foot pedal, cycling
the machine. The employee suffered a fingertip amputation and was treated
without hospitalization.
At 4:15 p.m. on September 1, 2020, an employee was lubricating a shaft bearing,
when the employee's finger got caught in the belt/pulley pinch point.  The
employee amputated a fingertip and was treated without hospitalization.
At 9:30 a.m. on September 3, 2020, an employee was replacing a screw in a cover
of an electrical panel. The employee was replacing the manufacturer's screws
that were rusted. Instead of using blunt-end screws, the employee was using
sheet metal screws, and in the process of affixing one of the screws, he drilled
into a conductor, electrifying the panel and causing an arc flash/blast. The
employee sustained severe burns on his arms, chest, and knees and was
hospitalized.
At 3:00 p.m. on September 10, 2020, an employee was cutting a downed tree into
smaller pieces with a chain saw.  The chainsaw kicked back and lacerated the
employee's left hand and chest.  The employee was hospitalized.
At 12:15 p.m. on September 4, 2020, an employee was monitoring a conveyor and
auto wrapping station. The employee reached into the rollers of the conveyer to
unwrap some plastic strips that were caught around the rollers. The employee had
a section of the plastic strips wrapped around his right index finger, and his
finger was pulled into the rollers. The employee suffered a right index
fingertip amputation and was treated without hospitalization.
On March 6, 2020, an employee working as a machinery maintenance technician for
a janitorial service had locked out an industrial-size meat grinder/auger to
clean and sanitize the equipment. The employee turned the power back on when he
noticed a piece of meat in the chute. The employee reached in with his bare hand
to remove the meat when the auger cutting blade struck his hand. The employee
amputated a finger to the second knuckle and was hospitalized.
At 5:45 p.m. on September 8, 2020, an employee was mowing the orchard area with
a brush hog. When the employee was found, he was near the brush hog, the tractor
was off and in gear with PTO disengaged. The employee had a laceration to his
right ear. It was determined that the employee had a myocardial infarction and
fell and hit the mower deck.
On March 20, 2020, Employee # 1 provided direct care to patients.  He was
infected with SARS-CoV-2 COVID-19, presumably from airborne droplets containing
SARS-CoV-2. Employee # 1 died from COVID-19 complications.
At 7:30 p.m. on August 31, 2024, an employee was placing insulation bags into an
insulation blow hopper powered by a gasoline Honda GX 690 engine. The engine
exhaust was piped outside the trailer, but the exhaust piping was not properly
sealed, and the muffler was rusted. As a result, carbon monoxide began to build
up inside the trailer. The employee was exposed to the dangerous levels of
carbon monoxide and was hospitalized to treat carbon monoxide poisoning. The
incident occurred due to inadequate exhaust system maintenance and failure to
ensure proper ventilation.
At 10:00 a.m. on September 3, 2020, an employee was running a rewinder/slitter
machine in jog mode to put a new paper roll on. The employee accidently turned
the machine to the higher rpm and had one hand placed on the roll of paper while
it was winding. The employee's arm was pulled in under the paper roll, resulting
in a fracture to the forearm. The employee was hospitalized.
At 9:00 a.m. on September 9, 2020, two employees were in a pickup truck operated
by Employee #1. While driving down an inclined, gravel access road, one of the
vehicle tires slipped and the vehicle went over an embankment and rolled.
Employee #1 was not wearing a seatbelt and was ejected from the vehicle and
killed due to crushing injuries when the vehicle rolled over Employee #1.  The
coworker was not ejected in the rollover and was not injured.
At 11:00 a.m. on May 29, 2020, Employee #1 was working for a roofing contractor.
Employee #1 was installing a new metal roof. Employee #1 fell approximately 32
feet from the roof to the ground. Employee #1 suffered head trauma, rib
fractures and lumbar fractures.  Employee #1 was hospitalized.
On June 28, 2020, Employee # 1 was transported to a medical center for the
treatment of COVID-19. She died on September 9, 2020 at 3:30 p.m. as a result of
COVID-19. Her employer reported the hospitalization of Employee # 1 on July 31,
2020, the date that the employer was notified by  a coworker, to the state OSHA.
Her employer reported the death to the state OSHA on September 10, 2020. The
Division initiated an onsite investigation on September 10, 2020 at 3:30 p.m.
On August 15, 2020, Employee # 1, who worked as a registered nurse at a
hospital, tested positive for COVID-19. He was hospitalized more than 24 hours
that day.
On July 30, 2020, Employee # 1 and Employee # 2 were employed as nurses for a
hospital. Both employees tested positive for COVID-19. On August 2, 2020,
Employee # 1 was hospitalized and released August 4, 2020. On August 2, 2020,
Employee # 2 was hospitalized and released August 6, 2020. The incident was
reported August 24, 2020 at 1:50 p.m.

An employee worked for a skilled nursing facility. The employee had been
off-work and scheduled to return on Monday, March 30, 2020. Prior to his work
shift, the employee called off work stating he was not feeling well. The
employee's job duties included non-medical, one-on-one interaction with
residents in the facility. On March 30, 2020, the employee reported to the
hospital where he was admitted. The employee tested positive for COVID-19 and
remained hospitalized until April 15, 2020 at which time he appeared to be
trending toward better health and refused additional medical services. On that
same date, the employee died from potential COVID-19 related pneumonia,
complicated by prostate cancer and his refusal to accept additional treatment.
The employee was reported to have had direct contact with confirmed or suspected
individuals who were infected with COVID-19. The employer did not have an
adequate respiratory protection program in place.
At 12:30 p.m. on October 21, 2020, an employee working as a truck driver for a
trucking company was assisting a coworker at a customer site. They were trying
to tow an electric pallet jack that was stuck between a shipping container and
the customer's loading dock using a second electric pallet jack. The employee
and the coworker tied a rope to the stuck PIV and tied the other end to the free
PIV. While the coworker operated the free PIV, the employee was standing next to
the stuck PIV. The rope on the stuck PIV snapped and struck the employee on his
right hand. The employee lacerated several fingers and fractured his index and
middle fingers, requiring hospitalization.
At 9:00 p.m. on April 23, 2020, an employee was preparing dough and decided to
observe a coworker that was operating the ball machine.  While the employee was
observing, some balls of dough fell from the rotating baskets.  The employee
opened the machine, that was on set up mode, to remove the dough.  The sprocket
caught his white coat sleeve and his arm, resulting in a severe arm laceration,
crush injury, open fracture, and radial artery injury.  The employee was
hospitalized for treatment.
At 8:00 a.m. on July 6, 2020, an employee was on a ladder while fire taping
sheetrock to an interior truss. The employee fell onto the concrete floor,
resulting in the employee becoming unconscious. Emergency services were called,
and the employee was hospitalized for treatment. The incident highlights the
importance of proper ladder safety and fall protection measures in the
workplace.
On October 17, 2020, Employee #1 and a coworker, employed by a residential
remodeling company, were part of a crew working at a customer's residence.  The
coworker felled a tree.  In falling, the tree struck Employee #1.  Emergency
medical services were called, and emergency dispatch gave the site employees
first aid instructions.  When emergency personnel arrived, they attempted
without success to revive Employee #1.  Employee #1, who had sustained blunt
force traumatic injuries, was killed.
On October 12, 2020, Employee #1, employed by a state highway department, was
operating a dump truck, Unit Number 000-0875, and working on a project to clean
up ditches along a parkway.  As he was driving, the right front tire dropped off
the edge of the road.  As Employee #1 attempted to pull back onto the road, he
lost control of the truck, which rolled over.  Emergency medical services
extricated the employee from the overturned truck and transported him by air to
a hospital.  The employee died from his injuries at the hospital approximately
two weeks later.  The investigation determined that Employee #1 was wearing his
seat belt and driving at an appropriate speed.
At 2:00 p.m. on October 22, 2020, Employee #1, employed by a road construction
company, was operating a broom tractor to sweep a road.  The tractor was rear
ended by a van.  Employee #1 was killed.
At 6:00 p.m. on October 8, 2020, an employee was loading a part into a machining
fixture. As the employee operated the clamping mechanism (with his right hand)
that holds the part into the fixture, the part moved, and the employee reached
with his left hand to support it, just as the fixture closed completely,
trapping the tip of his left index finger. The employee was hospitalized to
treat a left index finger amputation.
At 6:15 a.m. on May 22, 2020, an employee and a coworker were in the process of
transferring chemicals from totes on a delivery truck into tanks inside the
facility. The employee was responsible for hooking up the hose to the fill line
on the building and monitoring the transfer from inside the facility. The
coworker was responsible for hooking up the hose to the pump and tote inside the
truck. The employee accidentally hooked up the bleach hose to the fluoride fill
line, causing a reaction when the chemicals mixed. A toxic gas, presumably
chlorine, was given off and the employee inhaled the gas. The employee was
hospitalized from the inhalation of the toxic gas, and died from the injury.
At mid-day on October 16, 2020, a 28-year-old employee was working as a concrete
and terrazzo finisher for a poured concrete foundation and structure contractor.
He was finishing concrete. He was wearing gloves and a long sleeve shirt. He got
off work at 2 p.m. That afternoon, he experienced an outbreak of contact
dermatitis on his arms and possibly other body parts, resulting in a rash. At
5:00 p.m., he went to the hospital. He was hospitalized. The doctors believed
that exposure to concrete caused the contact dermatitis outbreak.
At 8:40 a.m. on June 12, 2020, an employee was changing filters on top of a
concrete silo. The employee had removed filters, when a coworker added air to
the system to check for leaks without PPE or engineering controls. The employee
lost consciousness after being exposed to Portland cement dust.  The employee
was treated without hospitalization.
At 6:54 a.m. on October 23, 2020, Employee #1, employed by a highway
construction company, was performing traffic control along a divided highway
while it was dark.  He was stopping traffic to allow dump trucks to back into
the job site.  A motor vehicle struck Employee #1, who sustained blunt force
traumatic injuries and was killed.
At 11:30 a.m. on June 17, 2020, an employee working as a truck driver for a
frozen food wholesale supplier was working at a food distribution warehouse. The
employee had just come back from a delivery route. After parking his truck on
dock 29, the employee walked inside the warehouse and proceeded to open the
roll-up door at the dock. The employee then lowered the gate of his trailer and
stepped onto the left side of the dock to and press the button which activates
the dock plate. At this point, the employee realized that he had not opened the
door of the trailer, so he walked between the raised dock plate and trailer door
to pull on the latch. As he reached for the handle on the door's latch, the dock
plate begins to lower pinning the employee between the raised dock plate and the
back door of his parked trailer.  Had the employee waited for the dock plate to
return to its resting place and disengage before attempting to open the trailer
door, the incident would have been prevented. The employee fractured his right
lower leg at his ankle and his right hand. The employee was hospitalized for
more than 10 consecutive days and required surgery.
At 7:00 a.m. on March 26, 2020, an employee was providing care to a patient in
Room 312, Bed 2, who was infected by the COVID-19 virus. The patient had been
presenting a fever for two days prior to arriving at the hospital, however the

fever of 101.6 degrees Fahrenheit at 5:30 a.m. prior to the employee beginning
his shift. The employee became infected with the COVID-19 virus and was
confirmed positive on March 30, 2020. The employee was admitted to the hospital
on the same day he tested positive and he was the only person in his household

At approximately 12:30 p.m. on April 19, 2020, an employee who had been working
as a Certified Nursing Assistant in the Immediate Intensive Care Unit was
hospitalized. The employee worked on the same floor as a coworker, who was also
hospitalized for COVID-19.  The employee did not interact with patients or
staff.  The employee was diagnosed with COVID-19, pneumonia, and a history of
asthma. Due to inconsistencies in reports, it is not possible to determine how
exposure may have occurred.

At 9:15 a.m. on October 12, 2020, an employee working as a laborer for a
petroleum refinery had hooked up 40 to 50 pounds of nitrogen to flush out the
sludge from piping. The employee started blowing out the pipe and heard a leak.
The leak was coming from the cam lock connection.  One of the securing gate
mechanisms allowed the nitrogen to go over to the cam lock.  The mechanism was
broken on the cam-lock connection, causing the nitrogen to leak in that area.
The employee took off his gloves and was inspecting the area/looking for the
reason for the leak by putting his hand near the broken area. The pressure from
the pipe caused a male plug to shoot out of the female connection and struck the
employee's right hand. The employee was hospitalized to treat a broken right
pinky finger.
At 2:30 a.m. on October 6, 2020, an employee was attempting to unjam the plastic
on the ZTECH air bubble film machine (cold chain bagger). The employee was
operating the ZTECH air bubble film machine to make plastic air bubble bags used
for cold chain shipping material. The machine uses flat rolls of air bubble
plastic, which gets folded and sealed to the customer's desired length and cut
in the middle of the seal to form the individual bags. The plastic needs to feed
under a metal bar to get to the portion of the machine where the blade cuts the
plastic and frequently jams at the bar location. At the time of the incident,
the plastic had jammed at the bar behind the blade and the employee reached in
through the exit area to attempt to dislodge the plastic. The machine was still
running when the employee performed this action. While his hand was still in the
end of the machine, the machine cycled, and the blade came down cutting the tip
of the employee's right index finger off.  The employee took himself to the
emergency room and later had surgery to attach a skin graft and close the wound
on the finger. The tip of the employee's right index finger was amputated but he
was not hospitalized.
At 2:00 p.m. on October 14, 2020, Employee #1 was on the roof, painting the
exterior of the building. Once finished, Employee #1 went to exit the roof,
using the extension ladder that had been previously set up to gain access to the
roof. As Employee #1 grabbed the ladder and put weight on it, the bottom swung
out and kicked out away from the building. This caused Employee #1 to fall
approximately 20 feet to the ground. Employee #1 was hospitalized to treat
multiple broken bones in the left leg.
At 10:45 a.m. on October 9, 2020, an employee was working at a petroleum
refinery. He was an apprentice rigger. He was working in the rigger shop. He was
using tongue-and-groove pliers, such as Channellock brand pliers, to disconnect
two pieces of pipe that had been bolted together into one length. The pipe had
been raised 6 in. to 12 in. (150 mm to 300 mm) by a crane. When the last bolt on
the top of the connector was removed, one section of the pipe was pulled up by
the crane. The other section fell to the floor. The ring finger on the
employee's left hand was pinched between the lower handle of the pliers and the
section of the pipe that was lifted and supported by the crane. The finger was
amputated. The employee was treated without hospitalization.
At 3:00 a.m. on October 11, 2020, an employee working for a plastics product
manufacturer was feeding cable into a molding machine. A portion of the
ceramic-like cover over the heating element inside the oven fell down exposing
the heating coil. The steel sheath over the cable became energized inside the
machine. As a result, the employee received an electrical shock to her right
hand and was hospitalized.
At 10:30 a.m. on March 31, 2020, an employee and a coworker, both working as
electricians and a journeyman mechanics for a graphic design service were
conducting maintenance work. They started preventative maintenance (PM) on the
High Density Storage System (HDSS). Both the employee and the coworker had been
trained to work on the HDSS system including an HSDD climbing class where this
process was reviewed.  In this training, both were taught the proper way to tie
off in the HDSS, using radios for communication and driving/operating the crane
in both manual and auto mode. The aisle has two cranes in operation. Crane #1
was parked, the crane aisle placed in maintenance, and the crane gate closed and
secured. This allowed Crane #2 to safely continue picking up skids while they
performed PM on Crane #1. The employee was the lead electrician/mechanic
providing direction to the coworker. One item on their PM list was painting the
chains, which required they lubricate the chains manually.  To do this, the
coworker was in Crane #1 operating the crane in manual mode. The employee was on
the lift station, seated above the crane on a cross support bar to perform
lubrication and test the vertical limit switch. He was correctly tied off to the
system. The employee and coworker communicated by radio. When they reached the
very top of the HDSS, the employee manually tripped the vertical limit switch to
perform the PM. After they had reset the limit switches, they communicated by
radio. The coworker thought he heard the employee tell him to go up, when he
actually said to go down. When the coworker moved the crane and lift station up,
the employee pinned his leg between the frame of the crane and the cross bar of
the lift station. The employee broke his leg and was hospitalized.
At 7:45 a.m. on September 10, 2020, an employee was running the Davenport five
spindle automatic screw machine. The employee was directly engaged in the
operation of making parts. The employee was standing next to his Davenport
machine, when he picked up his left hand and placed it on the machine, and his
left thumb was caught and broken.  The employee sustained a left thumb fracture,
requiring surgery.  He was hospitalized.
At 10:30 a.m. on June 8, 2020, an employee was working for a firm that
manufactured printing machinery and equipment. She was operating a Tesker model
440 cylindrical die thread rolling machine. She had long hair, and it got caught
in the machine. Her hair was pulled off. She suffered injuries to her scalp. She
was hospitalized.
At 1:30 a.m. on September 13, 2020, an employee working as a stock handler for a
returned to work after a half hour break. A coworker went to look for the
employee and found him unresponsive in his truck with the vehicle running. The
coworker pulled the employee from the truck and attempted to perform CPR and
called the EMS. The employee was taken to the hospital where he later died.
At 2:30 a.m. on October 27, 2020, an employee was travelling down the gangway of
a vessel. When he stepped off the foot of the gangway to the the apron he fell
into the water below. The employee drowned and was killed.
At 12:47 p.m. on October 28, 2020, an employee was exiting a customer shipping
door between his truck trailer and the docking area. He had just been assigned a
dock door and was heading to his truck when he was struck after another
semi-truck trailer hit a parked trailer. The employee suffered multiple injuries
and was killed.
At 1:00 p.m. on October 21, 2020, an employe working as a machine operator for a
recyclable products supplier was feeding cables into a wire stripper. The
employee claimed that the guard flipped up and the machine caught his glove
pulling his left hand into the machine blade. The employee required medical
treatment without hospitalization for a fracture to his middle finger and a
laceration to his index finger. The laceration resulted in an amputation to the
index fingertip approximately half-way into the nailbed.
At 2:53 p.m. on October 27, 2020, a temp employee had returned from a week long
absence from work and worked two days before he was taken to the emergency
department. The employee felt ill and took himself to the emergency room. The
employee later tested positive for COVID-19 and died.
At 1:15 p.m. on October 14, 2020, Employee #1 was carrying a hydraulic shore to
place into a trench when the shore unexpectedly opened. This caused the
employee's finger to be pinched in a nip point. As a result, the tip of the
employee's left-hand pinky finger was amputated. Emergency services transported
the employee to the hospital, where he was admitted for treatment.
An employee was caring for patients including COVID-19 infected patients when he
contracted the virus and subsequently died at 9:00 a.m. on June 3, 2020.
At 11:00 a.m. on October 28, 2020, an employee was operating a Husqvarna chain
saw felling a an 80 year old, approximately 40 foot tall dead oak tree. The dead
tree fell into 3 live trees which caused several large limbs to break off and
fall on top of the employee, killing him.
At 7:45 p.m. on October 24, 2020, an employee working for an air delivery
service was pushing an empty pallet with his foot. He caught his left foot
between an empty pallet and a steel frame. The employee was hospitalized to
treat a fractured foot.
At 7:00 p.m. on September 29, 2020, an employee, who was picking up aerosol can
products off the floor, tripped, causing him to fall forward.  His left hand
went past the machine guard, causing his left ring finger to jam into the
bearing and pulley on the exit feed side of the machine. The employee was
transported to OSF Sacred Heart Medical Center by a supervisor, where he was
treated for an avulsion and fingertip amputation and released.

cut metal angle iron. The employee had been employed by the employer for
approximately one year. He was the firm's only employee, and he was supervised
by the company's owner. As the employee operated the grinder, he held the lower
motor casing of the grinder and depressed the trigger with his rand. At the same
time, he held the motor casing near the gear casing and the rotating cutting
wheel with his left hand. The grinder kicked back, causing the employee to lose
control. The rotating cutoff wheel fractured. Parts struck the employee's left
arm. The employee suffered a lacerated wrist, and he was hospitalized for more
than 24 hours. The employer reported the accident to the Division at
approximately 4:10 p.m. on November 25, 2019, in compliance with reporting
requirements. The Division responded to the accident site at approximately 1:00
p.m. on December 3, 2019, and held an opening conference with the employer. The
grinder was not equipped with a side handle, required by the manufacturer to be
used at all times to maintain control of the tool. As well, the grinder was not
equipped with a type 1, closed, two-sided guard, again as required by the
manufacturer when a type 1 cut-off wheel was used, to protect the operator from
contact with the cutoff wheel.

unfrozen meat. The saw was used every day, 7 days a week, 7 to 8 hours a day.
The saw had an adjustable guard that could be raised or lowered to a desired
height. In this incident, the employee was using the saw to cut a
1-1/2-foot-long pork loin (1.5 feet, or 0.45 meters). To be cut, the loins were
placed on the saw carriage, where they rested against the saw's gauge plate. The
employee would then move the carriage from left to right. As the meat went into
the saw blade, it was cut, and the employee would use his left hand to remove
the cut pieces of meat while returning the plate carrier to the starting
position. In this incident, as the employee was cutting the loin, his left thumb
contacted the saw blade. His left thumb was partially amputated. He was
hospitalized. When interviewed, the employee stated he had adjusted the blade
guard to approximately 10 cm (4 in.) above the meat he was cutting. He did not
use a tool or other device to measure the distance; he used his eyes to
estimate. Another store in this chain was previously cited for a violation of
this standard, 29 CFR 1910.212(a)(3)(ii). This was covered in inspection number
1475307, citation number 1, item number 1. According to the employer's rules and
procedures, the guard on the saw is required to be lowered to typically 0.5 in.
(13 mm) above the meat being cut. Based on a statement from the firm's legal
counsel, there was no measuring tool used to ensure that the blade guard was
adjusted to the appropriate height. Meat cutters made visual determinations of
the gap. Employee interviews showed that the company's 0.5-in. (13-mm) guarding
rule was not being effectively communicated to or understood by employees.

said that she noticed that the board was not correctly positioned and so she

At 10:00 a.m. on December 9, 2020, Employee #1, employed by a roadway repair

At 4:30 p.m. on January 13, 2021, Employee #1 and a coworker were working at

Employee #1's left leg with the forklift tire. Employee #1 sustained a broken

An employee was working at a local outlet of a nationwide chain of big-box
November 21, 2020. The employee identified 10 coworkers he believed he could

An employee was working as a housekeeper in an assisted living facility when she

Employees were working in the boiler room of a veteran's medical center when it

An employee worked in the cuvette manufacturing area. The employee tested

At 11:58 p.m. on January 4, 2021, an employee was descending a staircase when he

At 9:00 a.m. on January 10, 2021, an employee who provided patient care in a

did not have Adequate Aerosol Transmissible Diseases policies and procedures in
place.
At 5:00 p.m. on January 31, 2021, an employee was loading a below ground pit
with dry sawdust when he dropped his cell phone into the pit. While attempting
to retrieve the cell phone, he fell into pit and was engulfed by the loose
sawdust which suffocated and killed him.
At 12:45 p.m. on February 2, 2021, Employee #1 was inspecting a well head while

On April 23, 2021, an employee who worked at a shellfish farming facility died

At 8:45 a.m. on March 5, 2021, an employee was operating the Perkins brand

At about 10:00 p.m. on December 4, 2020, an employee was working for a

At 12:45 p.m. on November 3, 2020, an employee was working for a firm that

At 2:30 p.m. on March 15, 2021, an employee was removing cut pieces of product

At 10:15 a.m. on October 15, 2020, Employee # 1 was standing by a crane.

At approximately 12:00 p.m. on December 9, 2020, an employee was working with

At 2:00 p.m. on March 19, 2021, Employee #1 was operating a diesel-powered

At 4:30 a.m. on March 16, 2021, Employee #1 was working at the Stanpac

admitted to the hospital and received surgery to reattach her fingertip and

including but not limited to: 	The machine was not under lockout / tagout while
the operator was checking the adjustment of the ice cream fill valve. 	The
employer had not performed periodic inspections of its lockout / tagout program.
The machine did not have guards in place to prevent access to the reciprocating
ice cream fill valve.
At 1:45 p.m. on December 3, 2020, an employee was working for a firm that sold

parts. She tripped over a toolbox on that was on the ground and fell. She

At approximately 2:43 p.m. on April 5, 2021, Employee #1, a 53-year-old slitting
