hospitalized for treatment of her infection on December 23, 2020.
At 2:00 p.m. on September 5, 2020, an employee was working as a dock worker in
the freezer dock area.  The employee attempted to move an 8410 end rider pallet
truck out of the way to make room for the work activities in the area.  The
employee was not assigned to operate the pallet truck and had attempted to move
it as a "walkie."  The directional controls are in reverse if you operate the
pallet jack as a "walkie," so when he attempted to move it, the pallet truck
pinned his right leg against the racking/wall in the dock area, causing a broken
leg.  The employee was hospitalized.
At 4:30 p.m. on October 1, 2020, an employee, a carpenter, was contracted to do
framing on-site. He had been tasked with cutting 1-inch by 6-inch siding.  The
employee was seriously injured when two of his fingers were amputated by the
circular saw he was operating.  He was treated and released at an Emergency Room
with subsequent follow-ups at a health clinic.
At 4:00 a.m. on February 21, 2021, an employee was at a customer location
displaying products. He needed to retrieve several jars stored in the bottom box
of a stack of boxes. In order to retrieve the jars, he tried to cut an opening
in the cardboard box with a box cutter instead of unstacking the boxes on top to
access the bottom box. His hand placement was in the direction of the blade. The
employee lacerated his left ring finger with the box cutter. He was treated
without hospitalization.
On June 14, 2021, an employee was working alone looking through granite remnant
samples when they fell on top of him, killing him.  The employee was found at
approximately 5 hours after coworkers had left in a sitting position between two
was found to be compliant with safety regulations regarding lavatory facilities,
eyewash stations, lead exposure, hazardous chemicals, and respiratory
protection. No violations were found, and the employer was cleared of
wrongdoing. A cease-and-desist letter was sent to the complainant for providing
false information.
At 8:30 a.m. on May 27, 2021, an employee attempted to join coworkers on roof to
begin work. The employee fell approximately twenty feet through insulation and
was killed.
At 1:30 p.m. on May 26, 2021, an employee was operating a stand-on zero-turn
lawn mower on an incline of approximately 15 degrees. The mower flipped backward
and landed on the employee's upper legs and abdomen. The employee sustained
multiple injuries, including a second-degree burn on the leg and a laceration to
the upper left leg. The employee was hospitalized for treatment.
An employee was assigned to the all-terrain vehicle unit and was performing
these duties on his last day of work prior to his illness on April 6, 2021. The
employee began experiencing flu-like symptoms, was administered a COVID-19 test
on April 8, 2021, and was advised to quarantine by his doctor. The employee
received a positive COVID-19 test results and was admitted to a medical center
on April 18, 2021. The employee died due to COVID-19 complications at 7:15 a.m.
At 7:45 a.m. on May 25, 2021, the employee was attempting to unclog an
industrial grain vacuum that was still energized and running. While doing so,
the agitator blades contacted his fingers, resulting in amputation of his right
index and middle fingers.  The employee was hospitalized for treatment.
At approximately 11:30 a.m. on May 31, 2021, an employee was removing stuck
chickens and chicken parts from the rotating carousel of a Meyn Maestro
Eviscerator while it was operating. Employee's left sleeve (near his hand) was
caught on the Meyn Maestro Eviscerator and he was pulled onto the pan below the
machine and against a horizontal support member for the eviscerator,  pinning
his body against the support and partially under the eviscerator's carousel. The
employee was killed from these injuries.
At approximately 12:45 p.m. on February 9, 2021, an employee returned from lunch
and was told by maintenance that the machine was ready for threading operations.
The employee began operating the Dubin #32 Roll Thredder set up on 1-318" X 36"
rowldbars running at approximately 100 RPM speed. The employee began to thread a
bar; he flipped the threaded side of the bar to the "V" shaped opening  with the
cut side spinning and exposed. The employee turned into the bar to take the bar
off of the threader and his shirt got caught in the threaded/cut side of the bar
behind the "V" away from the machine. The spinning bar wrapped the injured
employee's shirt and pulled him in the direction of the bar. The bar popped up
and then the injured employee reached over the bar with his left hand and the
bar snapped back into the "V" catching his left hand in between the "V" and the
bar.     The employee incurrred a fracture of the middle left finger, an
amputation of the left index finger, and lacerations of the top of the left
hand.  The employee was not hospitalized.
At 1:30 a.m. on February 4, 2021, Employee #1 was guiding a bundle of steel
tubes with his hands. The crane operator lowered the bundle of tubes, and they
shifted, pinching the finger of Employee #1.  Employee #1 amputated the tip of
the right middle finger and was treated without hospitalization.
At 10:00 a.m. on January 27, 2021, an employee climbed a ladder to access a
roof. At some point, the employee fell approximately ten feet and was killed.
At 12:30 p.m. on March 5, 2021, a mechanic was evaluating a malfunction of the
robot door as requested by the trim and drill department. The mechanic placed a
ladder alongside the pulley system, which supports the electric motor used to
move the door. While examining the system, the mechanic noticed the top, right,
outside pulley was loose. As the mechanic attempted to tighten the pulley bolt
with a wrench, the bolt sheared, causing the cable (with a 90 lbs.
counterweight) to fall. The mechanic's left hand was caught between the falling
cable and the frame. This resulted in the amputation of the left index finger at
the distal joint, as well as lacerations and a fracture to the left hand middle
finger. The employee was hospitalized for treatment.
An employee was working in the radiology department of a general hospital as a
lead, taking x-rays of patients and scheduling other imaging technicians. On
November 5, 2020, the employee tested positive for COVID-19 and began
self-treating at home. The employee's symptoms worsened and she was hospitalized
November 12-16, 2020, for treatment for COVID-19.
At 11:50 a.m. on April 7, 2021, Employee #1 was drilling holes into channel iron
using a mag drill on top of saw horses. While pushing a third channel over the
second, the channel iron fell off the saw horse and struck the employee's lower
right leg and foot. Employee #1 sustained a compound fracture to the lower right
leg and a fracture to the right foot. Employee #1 was hospitalized for
treatment.
At 6:00 p.m. on January 20, 2021, an employee who worked as a Patient Liasion
for a cancer care center died from COVID-19. The date, time and other details
leading up to exposure are not indicated in the narrative. Information regarding
engineering, administrative and personal protective equipment controls for
COVID-19 are not included in the narrative.
At 10:00 a.m. on April 17, 2021, an employee who worked as a construction
supervisor for a building contractor died from COVID-19 related complications.
His employer was contracted to perform construction work for an area nonprofit.
On March 25, 2021 the employee was informed by the nonprofit there was a
confirmed case of COVID-19 at the worksite. On April 5, 2021, the employee
tested positive for COVID-19. Information regarding engineering, administrative
and personal protective equipment controls for COVID-19 are not included in the
narrative.
At approximately 8:00 a.m. on May 29, 2021, an employee was riding a man lift
type elevator from the 4th floor to the ground floor.  The employee was found on
the ground floor and was unresponsive.  The employee was killed after a  head
injury.
In June 2020, an employee was part of a crew installing fiber optic
communication lines between two substations.  The employee was part of the crew
that unrolled and prepped cables ready for splicing. The land beneath the pylons
included arable and uncultivated land, some parts of which were dusty. Although
no soil disturbing activities were performed by the crew, the area was dusty,
and dust was kicked up by the work vehicles when driving and by the cable as it
was dragged over the ground. The employee inhaled spore of cocci and contracted
Valley Fever and showed gradually worsening symptoms starting about June 11-13,
2020. After initial misdiagnosis, the employee was diagnosed with Valley Fever
and given antifungal antibiotics and began to recover. The employer's 300 log
showed that he was away from work for 79 days. The employee was hospitalized for
treatment. Kern County has the highest rate of Valley Fever in the state, and
the employee had been working in the area for about a week before his onset
date. Since the employee had no reason to be in this area other than for work,
it was determined by the employer that this was a work-related infection. The
CALOSHA medical unit have produced a report and are also of the opinion that
this was a work-related infection.
At 2:10 p.m. on June 1, 2021, an employee was inspecting the seam on the top of
a Freightliner box truck when he fell nearly 12 feet from top of the truck. The
employee struck his head on a rock when he fell and was killed.
At 10:45 a.m. on April 29, 2021, an employee working as a meat cutter for a
wholesale grocery was cutting boneless pork chops. The employee was not
utilizing the push plate supplied to feed the meat product into the band saw. As
he used his right hand to feed the piece of meat into the saw his hand slipped
and contacted the sawblade. The employee was hospitalized to treat a lacerated
index finger.
At 7:30 a.m. on March 15, 2021, an employee was oiling gears and bearings on the
manure conveyor.  The employee's right index finger was caught in the exposed
gears.  The employee amputated the right index fingertip and was treated without
hospitalization.
At 5:30 p.m. on December 27, 2020, Employee #1 was headed to the Receiving Desk
to respond to an emergency call from family. A standup powered industrial truck
(PIT) was traveling in front of him when it abruptly stopped due to pallets
being pushed out in front of it by another PIT. Employee #1 rear-ended the
standup PIT, causing his left foot to become crushed between the two standup
PITs. Emergency services were called, and the employee was hospitalized.
Employees were working at a meat processing facility when a COVID-19 outbreak
occurred. The employer had implemented temperature checks upon entering and
required employees to wear face coverings and a bump cap with face shields.
Employee #1 was a Chopper Operator in the Chopper Blending Department. Employee
#2 was a Whizzard Operator/De-fatter for the Bone-In-Loin conveyor line.
Employee #3 was a Forklift Operator in the Distribution Center. Employee #4 was
a Quality Assurance Technician in Bacon Slice. Employee #5 was a Machine/Packout
fifteen minutes. The employee was retrieved and transported to the hospital. He
died from asphyxiation as a result of exposure to the argon. The San Diego fire
department reported the serious injury accident to DOSH San Diego at
approximately 9:00 a.m. The firm reported the fatality at approximately 10:00
foreman, had reviewed the operation of the forklift prior to working with the
forklift but did not review the forklift manual. The forklift manual states to
remain in the cabin in case of tip over and use outriggers to stabilize the
vehicle. The employee was hospitalized to treat four broken ribs.
At approximately 4:30 p.m. on April 6, 2021, an employee was preparing to paint
a damaged section of ductwork. The employee used a damaged extension ladder with
worn smooth feet to access the work area. Due to the slippery flooring, the
ladder slipped from under the employee, causing a fall. The employee struck his
head on a prepping table and sustained a head injury. The employee was
hospitalized for treatment.
At 8:41 a.m. on November 20, 2020, an employee struck the pavement with his
face, when he fell nine feet from a ladder while retrieving a transmission part
from a rack.  He was hospitalized to treat fractures to his eye socket and face.
At 3:15 p.m. on May 8, 2021, an employee working as a laborer for a poultry
processing facility was assigned to take over the new SensorX by Marel X-ray
inspection line while a coworker went to the restroom. If the machine detected
any possible bones, the chicken parts were sent to the rework part of the
inspection line. On the rework part of the inspection line, the employee removed
any chicken and bones and put it in a container. The employee then pushed the
deboned and inspected chicken parts onto the conveyor below the work surface by
pushing the chicken parts into a hole in the work surface. While looking away
from the work surface, the employee placed a hand into the hole in the work
surface. The employee's glove was caught by the conveyor belt which pulled the
employee's hand into the metal bar used to support the work surface. The
employee jerked his hand back resulting in removal of skin his a fingertip. The
employee received medical treatment without hospitalization. The skin could not
be used to close the wound so a medical decision was made to partially amputate
the fingertip in order to close the wound.
At approximately 9:00 a.m. on February 11, 2021, an employee was felling a tree
when the tree struck another tree, causing the butt end to kick up unexpectedly.
The falling tree struck the employee on the legs, resulting in a severe injury.
The employee sustained an amputation of the right leg and a fracture of the left
leg. The employee was hospitalized for treatment. This incident underscores the
importance of maintaining proper safety protocols during tree felling operations
and ensuring that the fall direction is controlled.
At approximately 11:30 p.m. on May 11, 2021, an employee working as a tractor
driver for a harvesting crew fell from a trailer while attempting to tarp a
loaded trailer in an agricultural field in Soledad. The fall resulted in a
fractured arm and leg. The employee was hospitalized for treatment. The employer
reported the incident to the Division on May 13, 2021, and the investigation was
opened on May 18, 2021.
At 12:15 p.m. on May 9, 2021, an employee working as a mechanic for an
automobile repair shot was trying to get the correct fuel/oxygen mix on a steam
cleaner mounted on a truck. The steam coil exploded due to overpressure and
sensors not working to shut machine down. The employee was struck by the hot
steam and was hospitalized to treat thermal burns to his face and scalp.
At 6:45 p.m. on March 16, 2021, an employee was cutting 6-foot boards using the
number one chop saw in the cut line at a sawmill facility in Madras, OR. The
employee's right thumb was at the point of operation when the saw was activated
by the leg/knee plunger, resulting in the amputation of approximately 0.50
inches of the thumb. The employer's safety director reported that the saw guard
was missing or broken at the time of the incident. The employee was transported
to St. Charles Madras for treatment, where it was determined that the thumb
could not be reattached. The employer will be conducting an accident
investigation and submitting a report to Oregon OSHA.
At 4:30 a.m. on May 13, 2021, an employee working as a heavy equipment operator
for an asphalt supplier was operating a loader. The RAP feed conveyor belt began
slipping at the head pulley. The employee exited his loader and attempted to
correct the slipping belt by throwing material (loose dirt) between the belt and
pulley while the conveyor was running. He climbed on the frame of the conveyor
system and used his gloved right hand to attempt to throw the dirt into the
machinery. The employee caught his glove in the nip point between the belt and
pulley which pulled his hand into conveyor. The employee fractured and bruised
his hand and fingers and was hospitalized.
At 4:00 a.m. on May 9, 2021, an employee working as a maintenance technician for
a smelter was hanging a breaker fuse. An arc flash occurred due to the power not
being fully turned off. The employee was hospitalized to treat burns including
2nd degree burns to his face and 3rd degree burns to his right hand.
At approximately 3:58 a.m. on May 17, 2021, an employee was working from an
extension ladder to install light fixture mounting brackets to interior roof
trusses approximately 16 feet above the showroom floor.  The employee utilized a
Werner brand 24-foot aluminum extension ladder.  The employee fell, presumably
from the extension ladder to the tile floor.  The employee was transported to a
local hospital to receive treatment for multiple blunt force injuries to the
head and body.  The employee later died from these injuries.
At 4:45 p.m. on February 16, 2021, Employee #1, while walking through the
basement of a workplace, was involved in a propane gas explosion. The explosion
caused severe second-degree burns to the employee's face and hands. Emergency
services were called, and the employee was transported to the hospital, where he
was admitted for treatment for the burns sustained during the explosion.
At 4:45 p.m. on February 22, 2021, an employee was moving cattle, when a cow
struck the employee's left leg.  The employee was hospitalized to treat a
fractured leg.
through the elevator doors and fall approximately 12 feet onto the elevator
platform below. The employee sustained fractures to the right ribs and pelvis
and was hospitalized for treatment.
At 3:04 p.m. on June 1, 2021, an employee was operating a Stihl Chainsaw to
clear trees from a site when the chainsaw kicked back and struck him the head.
The employee suffered a deep scalp laceration and a ruptured cerebral artery
which killed him.
At 1:00 p.m. on June 6, 2021, an employee was 15 feet high in a strangler fig
tree trimming branches with a chainsaw when he contacted an energized 14.4 kV
power line and fell to the ground. The employee died from electrical shock and
injuries resulting from the fall.
At 8:30 a.m. on May 21, 2021, an employee working as a heavy equipment operator
for a solid waste contractor was leveling the ground with a backhoe at a
landfill. The employee was sealing an aluminum deposit from two to three years
prior. The aluminum reacted with moisture in the ground releasing ammonia as the
operator began to level the ground. It could not be determined if the ammonia
overpowered the capabilities of the cartridge respirator or if the respirator
failed due to a broken seal or other reason. When the employee detected the
ammonia, he left the backhoe ran into the wind. The employee collapsed on the
ground and coworkers helped him to fresh air. A coworker who is also the
employee's son drove him to the hospital. The process is not routine since the
aluminum was buried above grade which has not been the case in over 5 years. It
was not possible to recreate the exposure. The employee was hospitalized with
scarring on his lung that has improved and he is expected to make a full
recovery.
Two employees were working for a public transportation system when they were
exposed to customers and coworkers who may have been infected with COVID-19.
Both employees contracted COVID-19 and were hospitalized but made a full
recovery.
At 5:00 p.m. on July 20, 2020, an employee and her coworkers were attending an
aggressive psychiatric patient. The employee was in charge of medication and was
attempting to inject the aggressive patient with a syringe. The patient was
distraught and fought against being injected and pushed the employee more than
once towards a set of steel lockers. The employee fractured her left ankle from
the impact against the lockers and was hospitalized.
An employee was working for a mental health treatment center when she left work
feeling ill and went to a regional medical center to get tested for COVID-19 on
May 26, 2021. The employee tested negative and was diagnosed with pneumonia. The
employee continued to experience COVID-19 related symptoms so she returned to
the medical center on May 29, 2021 tested positive for COVID-19, was
hospitalized, and was placed on a ventilator. The employee was released from the
medical center on June 24, 2021 .
At 4:00 p.m. on September 29, 2020, an employee was building props for a
movie/TV set. The employee was not acclimatized to the hot weather. The employee
suffered a heat-related illness and was hospitalized.
At 4:25 a.m. on May 7, 2021, Employee #1 knelt beside a maintenance employee to
observe repairs on a tape machine on Line 4. Upon standing, the employee grabbed
the north mast of the machine, and his left pinky finger entered a hole located
on the east side of the mast. While the tape machine was running, an operator
sent a box through, causing the floating upper head and pneumatic internal
column to move up to fit the box size and tape it. After the box passed, the
internal column returned down and contacted the employee's pinky finger inside
the facility. As the employee was focused on cutting the lock, an approaching
truck struck her from behind. The employee was hospitalized to treat a
concussion and fractures to both legs and required five surgeries.
An employee was working as a corrections officer at a correctional institute. On
August 30, 2021, he tested positive for COVID-19, and he was admitted to the
hospital. At 11:51 a.m. on September 10, 2021, he died of complications related
to COVID-19.
An employee had been working as a Manager at a dialysis center. The employee did
not have direct contact with patients. The employee developed COVID-19 related
symptoms and was tested on August 16, 2021. The employee tested positive for
COVID-19 and on August 31, 2021, she died. The date, time and other details
leading up to exposure are not indicated in the narrative. Information regarding
engineering, administrative and personal protective equipment controls for
COVID-19 are also not included in the narrative.
At 10:00 a.m. on August 25, 2021, an employee who worked as a Licensed Practice
Nurse (LPN) at a skilled nursing facility was hospitalized and tested positive
for COVID-19. The date, time and other details leading up to exposure are not
indicated in the narrative. The employer did not have an adequate respiratory
protection program in place.
An employee was working for an insurance agency that provided various services
to its members, such as insurance, travel, and roadside assistance services. He
worked in a large, three-story building as a roadside service dispatcher. He was
not vaccinated. On August 27, 2021, while at work, he was observed coughing. He
was instructed to go home. On or about August 29, 2021, he was said to have
sought treatment for symptoms associated with COVID-19 at a U.S. Department of
Veterans Affairs (VA) hospital. It was there that he was tested for COVID-19. He
learned that same day that his test results were positive. According to his next
of kin, the employee was sent home with medication to treat a pneumonia-like
illness and to convalesce. While at home on September 9, he fell or passed out
in the bathroom. Emergency medical services were called. The responders were
able to revive the employee temporarily, but while in transport or shortly after
arriving at the hospital, he died. His cause of death was reported as acute
respiratory failure with hypoxia due to COVID-19.  At 8:00 a.m., the employer
was notified on the following day, September 10, that the employee had died due
to complications of COVID-19. About three other employees have tested positive
at the worksite. The employer had not been able to speak with the employee
before he died to gather information on where he suspected he contracted
COVID-19.
At 8:25 a.m. on April 16, 2021, Employee #1 was operating a Rockwell
Manufacturing Co. table saw (Serial No. DD7063) in the basement of a batch plant
to cut a board for a shelf used to hold back hoses under the belt line. While
using a separate piece of wood as a push stick, the board being cut began to
rise. Employee #1 attempted to stabilize it with his free hand and made contact
with the unguarded saw blade, resulting in a partial amputation of his left
thumb. Emergency services transported Employee #1 to a hospital for treatment.
At 10:00 a.m. on June 4, 2021, Employee #1 was performing various production
tasks involving leather materials. While using a manually held rotary knife, the
employee's left index finger came into contact with the blade, resulting in a
fingertip amputation. The employee was hospitalized for treatment.
At 1:30 p.m. on July 1, 2021, Employee #1 was assisting with floor terrazzo
an industrial laundry was clearing a jammed sheet from a Jensen Jenfold Classic
S Model 5A0647 folding machine. The employee reached into the running machine
without activating the safety stop. The employee was hospitalized to treat
severe lacerations to the back of his left hand and tendon injuries.
Employee #1 who worked for a commercial truck dealership was hospitalized with
COVID-19.  The date of hospitalization was not specified in the narrative.  The
employee had been out of work for 2 weeks. The employer could not determine
where Employee #1 contracted the virus. Employee #1's family member notified the
employer of his hospitalization. Employee #2 last worked on December 9, 2020,
was tested on that same day and received a positive test result on December 11,
2020. On December 16, 2020, Employee #2 was hospitalized, which he reported to
his employer. Employee #2 was released from the hospital on December 21, 2020.
The employer stated that Employee #2's illness was possibly work related.
Employee #3 was also hospitalized but no details regarding his illness or the
date of hospitalization are indicated it the narrative. The job titles of the
three employees are also not indicated in the narrative. In addition,
information regarding engineering, administrative and personal protective
equipment controls for COVID-19 are not included in the narrative.
At 9:45 a.m. on July 29, 2021, an employee working as a sales worker for a
hardware store was stocking shelves. The employee fell off a ladder and was
hospitalized to treat a broken right arm.
An employee had been working as a Court Attendant for a court facilitating the
courtroom process using the Zoom application. On July 22, 2021, the employee
reported feeling ill and asked to leave work around noon. On July 23, 2021, the
employee called in sick. On July 26, 2021, the employee called in sick again and
tested for COVID-19. On July 28, 2021, the employee reported a positive test to
his employer. On July 31, 2021, the employee's former spouse notified the
employer that the employee had died sometime in the past 2 days. A friend
discovered the employee in his home after no calls or texts were returned.
Contact tracing showed that the employee shared a cubical/common desk with a
coworker who had tested positive for COVID-19. The employee used the area when
transferring Zoom calls and instructing court attendees. The employee and the
coworker covered each other's duties during breaks. During the week of July 12,
2021, the coworker's spouse and stepdaughter became ill with flu-like symptoms
but both rapid and PCR tests were negative for COVID-19. During the week of July
19, 2021, the coworker began to feel ill with the same symptoms but disregarded
the symptoms due to his family's test results. The coworker informed other
coworkers of his illness but that his family had tested negative. On July 22,
2021, both the employee and coworker reported being ill, but only the left work
early and did not return. The coworker tested positive for COVID-19 via a rapid
test on July 26, 2021, but his PCR test came negative. The employee and coworker
had worked in close prolonged proximity on July 20, 2021, and July 21, 2021. The
employee reported having the same symptoms as the coworker and his family. Due
to the conflicting test results, it is unclear who the employee contracted
COVID-19. No causes or contributing factors could be identified leading up to
the illness.
At 9:33 a.m. on July 10, 2021, an employee working as a part time service
technician for a tire shop was responsible for changing tires on customer
vehicles. The employee would take the removed tires, know as "dead" tires, and
stack them on a tire dolly. Once the dolly is filled to the top the employee
would then unload it into a tire container located beside the building. On July
10, 2021, the employee advised the employer that when he was transporting the
dead tires on the dolly to the container he hit his leg on the dolly and
sustained a small cut on his shin. The injury developed into cellulitis. He said
he had developed cellulitis on this leg in the same spot about 5 years ago from
a football injury. On July 15, 2021, the employee failed to show up for his
shift. The employer reached out to the employee who stated he was in the
hospital since July 13, 2021.
At 5:04 p.m. on June 2, 2021, an employee was struck by a large steel beam that
fell over top of him. The employee was killed after being pinned between the
beam and a semi tractor trailer truck.
At 4:30 p.m. on May 21, 2021, an employee working as an electrical maintenance
technician for a fabricated metal products manufacturer was installing temporary
electrical circuits. The employee was installing two new 480-volt circuits for
portable air conditioning units in the Koch oven area. The specific work
involved opening and working inside live 480 volt switch gear, terminating wires
in the gear and installing new fuses in a disconnect. This was part of regularly
assigned work duties for the employee. The switch gear faulted and caused an arc
flash. No witnesses were working in the area at the time of the incident. The
employee was hospitalized to treat burns to his left hand, wrist and lower arm.
At 12:30 p.m. on July 30, 2021, an employee was processing truck dispatch
tickets in an office when a coworker found him unresponsive. The employee had
died of a possible heart attack.
At 5:50 p.m. on May 15, 2021, an employee working as a machine operator for a
meat processing company was attempting to clear a jam on the Ross Slicer. The
employee's hand contacted the blade of the slicer. The employee was hospitalized
to treat an amputated left thumb.
At 3:45 a.m. on July 20, 2021, an employee working as a stock handler for a pet
supply retailer was assisting or providing tips to a new coworker. The employee
placed her right hand near a conveyor when the powered rollers caught her hand
and pulled it into the machinery. The employee was trapped by the machine
requiring that the rollers be removed to free her hand. The employee was
hospitalized to treat friction burns to her fingers and internal damage that
required surgery to her ring finger.
An employee was working for a fruit grower and packager when he contracted
COVID-19. The employee was hospitalized with on May 17, and he was discharged to
injuries.
At 9:20 a.m. on February 3, 2021, Employee #1 was working for a roofing
contractor.  Employee #1 was walking on a roof picking up nails. Employee #1
slipped on a nail and fell from the roof. Employee #1 suffered fractured ribs
and was hospitalized.
At 10:00 a.m. on July 16, 2021, an employee was killed due to burns from a fire
following an explosion that occurred while he was welding. The source of the
explosion is unknown, but believed to be gases from the tank farm where he was
working or welding gases ignited by either a vehicle or a welding machine.
At 12:00 a.m. on July 17, 2021, an employee operated an Ingersoll Rand Carryall
1500/1700 off-road on the night shift to assist with security of a jobsite. At
some point, the vehicle rolled over, ejected, and rolled onto the employee. The
employee was killed by crush injuries.
At 4:20 a.m. on May 14, 2021, an employee working as a machine operator for a
screen printer stuck his right arm between pallets to check a T-shirt ink
machine. A coworker turned on the machine and caught the employee's arm between
the machine and the pallets. The employee was hospitalized to treat a broken
arm.
At 8:30 a.m. on April 10, 2021, an employee was 15 to 20-feet up in a dead tree
that he was cutting down when it fell over. The employee was killed when he made
contact with the ground.
At 7:30 a.m. on June 17, 2021, Employee #1 was attempting to clear a jam in the

meat and chicken departments. Employee #1 sustained a broken leg and multiple

At approximately 7:00 a.m. on June 25, 2021, an employee who was sorting

At 4:00 p.m. on February 12, 2021, an employee working for a country club was

Two correctional officers and one licensed vocational nurse were hospitalized

At 1:03 a.m. on August 2, 2021, three employees were setting up for the night

At 8:26 a.m. on July 31, 2021, Employee #1 was undergoing on-the-job training

At 6:45 a.m. on May 23, 2021, Employee #1, a shift manager at a limited-service
employee, wearing gloves, attempted to wipe the surface area that had just been

The employee was treated but not hospitalized.

At 7:45 a.m. on August 24, 2021, an employee was operating a Caterpillar D6K2

At 3:30 p.m. on August 17, 2021, an employee was standing on the bucket
attachment of a skid-steer tractor facing the operator compartment and

injuries to his chest and neck and died.
At 2:30 p.m. on August 20, 2021, an employee (Mechanic) was working at  the tank
farm area of a commercial gas station prior to a concrete pour. The employee was
working with three coworkers, including his supervisor, spreading gravel before
the pour. The employee was standing in the shade when he collapsed. Coworkers
started CPR and called emergency responders, who worked on the employee and
transported him to the hospital. The employee died at the hospital as a result
of personal medical conditions.
At 8:00 p.m. on May 23, 2021, Employee #1 was clearing scrap bags as part of a
employee attended a family get together the weekend prior to becoming ill.
An employee was working conducting computer training alone in the office of a
car dealership when he contracted COVID -19 and subsequently died from his
infection at 8:00 a.m. on September 15, 2020.
An employee was working in a meat processing and packaging facility and was at
home when he began having symptoms of COVID-19. The employee  subsequently died

At approximately 9:20 a.m. on December 3, 2020, an employee was operating a pin
press machine when the employee's finger became caught between a pin piece and
the ram of the machine. This incident resulted in the amputation of the
fingertip and was treated without hospitalization.
An employee was working in a warehouse when he contracted COVID-19. The employer
records indicated that there were no positive cases of COVID-19 seen in the
building for 14 days prior to the employee becoming ill and receiving a positive
test. The employee had attended a family reunion at his home seven to ten days
prior to his positive diagnosis. Family that attended the reunion had come from
out of state and several that attended became ill with COVID-19 afterwards.  The
employee died at 8:00 a.m. on November 15, 2020, from complications of his
infection.
At approximately 6:30 p.m. on December 3, 2020, an employee was operating a
hydraulic trimming press when the two hand control devices (guards)
malfunctioned. While attempting to remove a part from the point of operation,
the employee inadvertently activated one of the hand control devices. Due to the
malfunction, the machine cycled with only one hand control device engaged,
resulting in the amputation of two fingers inside the press's point of
operation.  The employee was hospitalized for treatment.
At approximately 10:00 a.m. on December 4, 2020, an employee was a Meat
Cutter/Service desk employee who last worked on November 6, 2020.  The employee
never returned to work after experiencing Covid-19 like symptoms.  The employee
went to the hospital on November 23, 2020 after experiencing shortness of
breath.  On November 23, 2020, the employee was admitted to the hospital and
subsequently tested positive for COVID-19.  The employee died on December 4,
2020, attributed to complications from COVID-19.
At approximately 2:10 a.m. on December 3, 2020, Employee #1, a 40-year-old male
forklift operator, was transporting scrap metal to the storage yard. After a
brief conversation with another powered industrial vehicle (PIV) operator, the
employee pulled away, grasping the vertical roof support of his forklift cab.
During this movement, his left hand became trapped between the support beam of
his forklift and the open cab door of the coworker's vehicle, resulting in
significant crushing injuries.  He also sustained lacerations to his left hand.
Employee #1 was hospitalized and required surgical amputation of his left index
finger.
At approximately 3:00 p.m. on December 6, 2020, an employee was fitting a piece
of the metal plate onto a marine barge. Metal plate struck the scissor lift,
causing the employee to fall. The employee fell to the ground and died from a
brain injury.
At approximately 9:00 a.m. on December 8, 2020, an employee along with a
coworker was breaking up clumped corn inside a grain silo at a dry corn milling
facility.  The concrete silo had a sloped bottom, was approximately 120 feet
tall and 50 feet in diameter with a capacity of approximately 200,000 bushels.
During this time, a coworker left the silo and surrounding area to perform other
work while the employee continued working inside the silo, alone.   Later that
morning, it was discovered that the employee was missing, and at 9:00 AM
emergency services were contacted and a confined space rescue proceeded.  At
approximately 4:30 PM, emergency responders located the body of the employee in
the silo.  The employee had been engulfed in the corn.  No attendant was present
when the employee was working inside the silo.  The cause of death was
determined to be blunt force trauma of the neck and asphyxiation due to corn
engulfment.
At 6:30 p.m. on October 27, 2020, an employee working as a dough maker for a
grocery store was cleaning the dough maker machine. The employee failed to turn
off the machine and disconnect the power source before cleaning. The employee
reached inside the machine and crushed his right hand between the moving tines.
The employee was hospitalized to treat a fractured hand.
At approximately 4:00 a.m. on December 5, 2020, an employee contracted COVID-19
and later died from complications from the virus.
At approximately 9:45 p.m. on December 4, 2020, an employee was performing
typical RN duties: assisting with deliveries, triage, etc. The employee
contracted COVID-19 and was hospitalized.
At approximately 9:00 a.m. on December 7, 2020, an employee was moving by
forklift heavy screens from one location to another. The employee did not secure
the heavy load properly and as the employee was directing the forklift operator
to lower the load, the load came off the fork striking the employee causing him
to strike his head on the blue dumpster and then concrete. The employee was
killed.
At 4:06 p.m. on December 4, 2020, Employee #1, employed by a framing
construction contractor, was working at the construction site for a new
three-story residential structure.  He was attempting to lift a framed exterior
wall into place.  The wall was too heavy, and it fell onto the employee.
Employee #1 sustained blunt force traumatic crushing injuries and was killed.
At 4:59 p.m. on November 19, 2020, an employee was cutting frozen turkey meat
with a Hobart vertical bandsaw for a customer.  The employee had his left hand
in close proximity to the point of operation and amputated the tip of the left
index finger.  The employee was hospitalized.
At 1:00 p.m. on August 31, 2020, an employee was working as a machine operator
for a firm that manufactured metal products. Her facility made metal chains and
fittings for lifting. The incident happened on the facility's Allen model number
3 variable speed multi-spindle drill press, with employer's machine number
F43417. At the site, it was referred to as the large Allen drill. It came to the
site in 2015. The employer used the large Allen drill to drill, ream, tap, and
bore holes in cast and forged metal components. The drill originally had four
spindles, but due to the increased difficulty of finding parts, the employer had
removed a spindle. Each spindle had a three-sided Plexiglas shield on an
adjustable arm for positioning in front of the operating drill. These shields
were easily moved and did not have an interlock that would stop spindle rotation
when the shield was positioned away from the point of operation or other moving
parts. The employee was setting up the drill's far-left spindle to run a job. As
she was adjusting its speed, a strand of her hair became caught and entangled at
the top of the rotating shaft. Her shirt also became entangled, and the machine
picked her up off the floor. She couldn't reach the ON/OFF button. Eventually
she got free, possibly when the tapered drill bit came out. She suffered a
traumatic scalping injury, from just above her eyes to the back of her head. She
lost her right ear, except for the ear lobe, and a chunk was taken out of her
left ear. The small finger on her left hand was fractured and lacerated. She
suffered lacerations to her stomach and torso areas. She was taken by ambulance
to a hospital, where she underwent surgery to reattach her scalp. The surgery
did not take, so she had to undergo debridement and have skin grafted from her
thighs to her head. By late 2020, she had had seven surgeries and continued
hyperbaric treatments. She faced further plastic surgeries. Her small finger
also required surgery.
At 7:00 p.m. on December 1, 2020, an employee was working as a utility worker
for a sawmill. A coworker operating the TBL sawmill had called the employee to
clear a jam on the machine. The TBL sawmill cuts slabs from logs. The employee
opened the door to the saw blades to unjam a slab with the machine energized
when his hand was struck by the rotating head saw. The employee amputated a
finger to the first knuckle and was hospitalized.
At 5:20 a.m. on December 7, 2020, Employee #1 and three coworkers, employed by a
platform and hit it with a sledgehammer when one of the studs broke sending the
employee to the ground. The broke both ankles and was hospitalized.
At 4:00 p.m. on November 23, 2020, an employee who had worked for a skilled
nursing facility was hospitalized with COVID-19. The employee's title or job
duties are not indicated in the narrative. The date, time and other details
leading up to exposure are also not indicated in the narrative. The employer did
not have an adequate respiratory protection program in place.
At 11 a.m. on December 22, 2020, an employee was attempting to free a hung-up
tree. The hung-up tree released and whipped back onto the employee. The employee
died due to blunt force trauma.
At 4:00 p.m. on December 21, 2020, Employee #1 and coworkers, employed by a
water and sewer line construction company, were attempting to repair a
residential sewer line that was back flowing.  While they were in the trench
they had dug, a trench wall collapsed.  Employee #1 was caught in the collapsing
material and fatally crushed.
An employee was working as a social worker for a county behavioral services
department. The employee teleworked most days but was mandated to be in the
office one day per week. Occupancy levels in the office were approximately 50
percent and face masks were worn at all times. The three employees had separate
ambulance. She was treated at the hospital until she died at 10:00 p.m. on
January 24, 2021. Initial information indicated that although the employee did
not provide care to COVID-19-positive patients, she was exposed to a COVID-19
positive coworker. There were no known cases of COVID-19 in her immediate
family. She might have had symptoms as early as December 24, 2020.
At 11:45 a.m. on January 12, 2021, Employee #1, standing in the basket of a boom
lift, was repositioning the basket while using a paint hose connected to a
ground pump. The hose was slung over the basket railing. During the
repositioning, the spray line ruptured, causing high-pressure paint injection
into the employee's right thigh. Emergency services transported the employee to
the hospital, where he was admitted and treated for the injury.
At 1:15 a.m. on January 24, 2021, an employee was training a coworker how to
operate a baler after receiving a maintenance request on the machine. The
employee climbed up and on the baler while showing the coworker how to take care
of the request. The baler activated and the door opened pinning the employee
between the door and the metal bar on the side of the machine which asphyxiated
and killed him.
At 9:15 a.m. on Tuesday, January 26, 2021, two employees were working for a
landscaping service. The two employees were on their way to begin tree trimming
operations. They were traveling in a Genie model S-65 4 x 4 articulating boom
aerial lift, with serial number S60H-38745. When the aerial lift went over a
septic hole, the lift tilted and started to fall over. The two employees jumped
from the lift before the boom contacted the ground. They jumped approximately 20
feet (6.1 m). One employee suffered a fractured right leg. He was hospitalized.
The other employee suffered no injuries. The firm's owner said that the
employees working in the aerial lift had received no fall protection training.
The limbing foreman said that the employer never provided any type of fall
protection training to employees that used the aerial lifts. The owner said that
the firm's employees normally climbed trees to top them and used the aerial lift
only about once per month.
At 11:00 a.m. on January 21, 2021, Employees #1 and #2 and two coworkers,
employed by an energy supply company, were responding to a call from a
contractor who was excavating a 200-foot water line addition to a meat market, a
multiemployer construction project.  The contractor had struck an underground
power line between transformer 1 and transformer 2 while excavating.  The power
line break caused power to be lost at the meat market and a neighboring
facility.   The four energy supply company employees were working to repair the
broken underground power lines.  Employee #2 shut the power off at the pole and
placed grounding straps on the secondary compartment of transformer 1.  Employee
#2  joined Employee #1 on the west side of the excavation while their coworkers
worked elsewhere.   When the power was interrupted, a generator in the facility
next door started automatically and began providing power to the facility's
office.  Approximately 30 minutes later, an employee from the neighboring
facility threw a manual switch connected to a generator to supply electricity to
the facility's warehouse.  The electricity back-fed through the ungrounded
transformer 2 to where Employees #1 and Employee #2 were working.  Both
employees received an electric shock from the backfeed.  Employee #1 was killed
by electrocution.  Employee #2 sustained severe burns to the hands.  Employee #2
was transported by emergency services to the hospital, where he was admitted for
treatment of the electrical burns.
An employee was working for a firm that engaged in the rolling, drawing, and
extrusion of aluminum. The firm made windows and doors. The employee worked as
an industrial truck and tractor operator. He drove a forklift truck on the
second shift within the facility. His last day worked was December 2, 2020. He

2020. The results came back the following day, December 8, 2020. They were

the following day, January 22, 2021, OSHA contacted the corporate safety manager
to conduct a remote interview. The safety manager reported that there had been
additional COVID-19 cases at the facility.
An employee was working as a certified nursing assistant in the positive

11, 2020, which resulted in a positive COVID-19 test. The employee was admitted
to the hospital on December 23, 2020, was released from the hospital on December
28, 2020, and readmitted on January 6, 2021. The employee subsequently died on
January 25, 2021 from acute respiratory failure due to COVID-19.
At 5:00 p.m. on December 13, 2020, Employee #1, employed by an electrical and
wiring installation company, died on the job.  During the subsequent
investigation, the medical examiner stated that the employee's fractured ribs

feeling sick, and having rib pain.  No coworkers witnessed any work-related
injury.

At 12:15 p.m. on November 12, 2019, an employee was placing polyester material

At 12:00 p.m. on January 22, 2021, Employee #1 and a coworker, employed by a

At 4:36 p.m. on January 29, 2020, Employee #1 was assisting in the operation of

At  7:15 p.m. on January 29, 2021, an employee was cleaning shot off a flat

hand was caught between the plate and the rollers in a pinch point.  He received
crushing injuries to the four fingers of the left hand, resulting in amputations

At 11:30 a.m. on January 18, 2021, Employee #1 was climbing a fixed ladder on an
open-top rail car to take a picture of the empty railcar. As the employee
reached the top, his hand slipped off the top ledge, causing him to fall 18 feet
to a rock/dirt surface. The fall resulted in a spinal fracture at the L1
vertebrae. Weather was not a contributing factor. Contributing factors may
include lack of engineering controls and the employee's position on the fixed
ladder. The employee was hospitalized for treatment.
At 11:35 a.m. on August 12, 2020, an employee was preparing to cross a roadway
to remove refuse from a residential property. The employee stepped in to the
path of an oncoming truck traveling in the opposite direction of the refuse
hauler. The employee was admitted and treated at the hospital for a compound
fracture of the leg below the knee.
On January 24, 2021, an employee who worked for a new car dealership died from
COVID-19. The employee's family member reported the employee's death to the
employer on an unspecified date. The date that the employee last worked is not
indicated in the narrative, but it is known that on that date the employee
called into work around 11:00 a.m. and left a message with the receptionist. The
employee worked independently which included working outside washing cars and
moving vehicles from one lot to another. The employee was not found to have
potentially infected any coworkers. The employer reported a cluster of COVID-19
cases at the dealership but said the employee had not been in close contact with

Around the time the employee contracted COVID-19 and up to two weeks prior,
Employee #2, Employee #3 and Employee #4 were hospitalized. Employee #5 was

without determining that the structure was capable of supporting the load.
A 69-year-old employee was working as dietary aide at a nursing care or skilled
nursing facility. She tested positive for COVID-19 prior to starting her shift.
She did not return to work. At 8:00 a.m. on December 8, 2020, she died.
At 6:00 p.m. on November 24, 2020, an employee was replacing liner material into
the machine. The employee removed his hand from the brake that holds the machine
static.  The weight of the die of the machine caused the employee to lose his
grip on the adjustment wheel that is used to index the liner material.  The
employee attempted to grasp the belt of the machine to stop it from turning and
inadvertently placed his finger into the nip point at the belt behind the
adjustment wheel. The employee amputated his right index fingertip.  The
employee was treated without hospitalization.
At 4:00 p.m. on January 11, 2021, Employee #1 from Police Department #1
responded to a vehicle crash when one of the drivers involved in the crash
opened fire on him with an AK-47 killing him instantly. The driver then car
jacked a vehicle and took off toward the airport. Employee #2 from and Employee

Employee #2, killing him. Employee #3 was injured in the leg and hospitalized.
As the driver attempted to flee in the car a second time, he struck Employee #4
from Police Department #1 with the car killing him.  See also Investigation
Summary ID 132439.
At 10:30 a.m. on November 28, 2020, an employee working for a sheet metal
contractor was installing ventilation grating. The employee slipped and fell on
the unsecured grating. The employee was hospitalized to treat a fractured ankle.

An employee was a laundry worker who tested positive for COVID-19 on November
23, 2020.  The employee was initially asymptomatic, subsequently became
symptomatic, was hospitalized on December 1, 2020, and died on  January 19,
2021, from the viral infection SARS-CoV-2.
At 10:45 p.m. on January 26, 2021, an employee was working in the parking lot
doing COVID testing. A pediatrician from out of town came to volunteer at the
next door facility, but was told no. He returned unexpectedly one week later
with a gun, held a hostage, and then killed the hostage, the doctor, and
himself. During the incident, many employees from the neighboring business
managed to escape and enter the ER's facility. The ER provided shelter and
police communication to escaped employees. The employee experienced a fatal
gunshot wound to the head.
On October 30, 2020, an employee working for a window cleaning service was
washing windows from a roof. The employee stepped off the edge of the roof and
fell 10 feet to the ground below. The employee was hospitalized to treat a
broken neck.
An employee was working in the laundry room of a nursing home when he contracted
COVID-19. The employee quarantined at home and subsequently died in his home at
2:00 p.m. on December 28, 2020.
At 11:00 a.m. on January 28, 2021, an employee inspected a kitchen exhaust
system that leaked grease. At some point, the employee fell approximately twenty
feet through the ceiling drywall tile, received traumatic head and body injuries
with severe bleeding and was killed.
At 2:30 p.m. on January 18, 2021, Employee #1, a machine operator at a metal
fabrication business, was operating a Verson mechanical punch press (model B510,
serial no. 9079) equipped with tooling to form tubular handles. The employee was
using a foot pedal control to operate the punch press when the right ring finger
and pinky finger were caught in the punch press tooling. The punch press was not
equipped with safeguarding devices to prevent cycling when the employee reached
into the point of operation area. The employee sustained partial amputations to
both fingers. The employee was hospitalized for treatment.
At 9:15 a.m. on Saturday, January 23, 2021, an employee was working for a firm
that manufactured heavy gauge metal tanks. He was working as a helper, mechanic,
and repair technician. The firm operated a metal fabrication facility at this
location. The employer had 24 employees at this facility and approximately 100
employees throughout the United States. The employee and a coworker were working
on a Roundo plate roller. The plate roller was located at the facility's north
wall by the bay door. The plate roller was operated with a pendant control, but
there were electrical issues with the control. The coworker was doing electrical
work while the employee cleaned the plate roller. The coworker, not knowing that
the employee was cleaning the rollers on the plate roller, started up the
machine. More than one finger on the employee's left hand was caught in the
rollers. The employee suffered the amputation of all or part of the middle and
index fingers on his left hand. The employee was taken to the hospital for
treatment. He was hospitalized. During a visual inspection, the CSHO noted there
was no guard for the point of operation for the roller. A control pendant was
lying on the roller, bearing a tag that stated "out of service," with initials
and dated 1-25-21. The control buttons to the pendant had no labeling on them to
identify their direction. The CSHO inspected the electrical cord for the
roller.t had black tape wrapped around the cord. Upon verifying that the roller
was disconnected, the CSHO removed the black tape. Underneath, the inner cables
were revealed, but no exposed wiring.
At 3:00 p.m. on January 27, 2021, Employee #1 was cleaning a run-off/drip of
plastic from a PTI extrusion system machine (model RJ781830). After hanging up
the removal tool, Employee #1's left hand was caught between two moving rollers
on the machine. The incident resulted in the amputation of the left hand's fifth
("pinky") finger and a partial amputation of the fourth finger. The employee was
transported to the hospital for admission and treatment.
An employee was admitted to the hospital on December 13, 2020, due to COVID-19
exposure Employee was initially admitted to the hospital from positive testing
on COVID-19 and was later tested negative. However, the employee had
complications from existing pneumonia and was worsened, and was later put on a
life support system. The family members later decided to stop the life support
system at 1:00 p.m. on January 18, 2021, and the employee died.
At 11:48 a.m. on January 28, 2021, an employee was working as part of a
technical team in the projection room of a small theater in an industrial
electronics facility. The employee experienced  a medical emergency and died.
At 8:30 p.m. on January 21, 2021, an employee working as a heavy equipment
operator for a refrigerated warehouse and storage facility was driving a Raymond
Model 8410 Pallet Jack (SN: 841-13-13344). The employee was driving through the
doorway leading to aisle 60 from the alpha (A) dock. As the employee went to go
through the door he slowed down and was honking the horn in accordance with his
training. As the employee was traveling west through the door, a coworker was
traveling east from aisle 60. The employee noticed the coworker as he was
turning into the doorway causing him to swerve to the right to avoid a
collision. In doing so, the employee drove the pallet jack through a puddle of
water, which the pallet jack's wheels are not equipped to handle. This caused
the employee to lose control of the pallet jack. The employee attempted a soft
stop of the pallet jack, and when that failed, he leapt from the pallet jack to
perceived safety. As he went to leap, his ankle contacted the barrier pole to
the right of the door. The bumper of the pallet jack then connected with the
employee's foot smashing it into the pole. The employee was hospitalized to
treat a fractured ankle, tibia and fibula.
An employee was a correctional officer guard in the dental triage area of the
medical unit. His job was to ensure that prisoners arrived for their appointment
on time. Sometimes he would go to their housing unit to get them and other times
they would be brought to him by a CO. Inmates who came to the dental area were
tested for COVID-19 with a rapid test and taken away to quarantine if positive.
Once negative they could go in to see the dentist. Inmates and staff both wore
surgical masks. Getting prisoners into holding cells while they awaited the
results of the rapid tests would put prisoners and correctional officers within
