At 8:30 p.m. on February 24, 2021, Employee #1 was conducting a mold change
using an overhead crane. The 22-ton mold was left suspended while the employee
was cleaning debris from it. While positioned between the suspended load and
another stationary mold, the employee switched the crane pendant control from
one hand to the other. A button on the pendant was inadvertently pressed,
causing the crane to move. The employee was struck by the suspended load,
resulting in injuries to his right shoulder and ribs. The employee was
hospitalized.  The incident occurred as a result of the suspended load and the
stationary mold.
At 11:54 a.m. on December 7, 2020, Employee #1, a scaffold erector employed by a
plastering contractor, was erecting a metal frame scaffold on the north
elevation of a new multifamily mixed-use building under construction. The
section of the scaffold was near high-voltage conductors located approximately
10 inches from the scaffold. Although an agreement had been made between the
general contractor and plastering contractor to avoid completing the scaffold in
this area until the power lines were removed, work proceeded in this hazardous
location. While securing plywood to the scaffold, Employee #1 came into contact
with or was in close proximity to the conductor, resulting in an electrical arc.
The employee suffered electrical burns to the arms and hands and was transported
to the hospital for admission and treatment.
At 5:45 a.m. on January 16, 2021, Employee #1 was asked by a customer to cut a
meat bone approximately the size of a tennis ball. The employee held the meat
bone with both hands and cut it against the bandsaw blade in the air. While
cutting, the employee amputated his left ring finger and lacerated the tip of
his thumb. The incident occurred while using a Biro Model 33434 Power Meat
Cutter bandsaw machine. The employee was transported to the hospital for
admission and treatment.
At 10:00 a.m. on April 26, 2021, an employee was mowing grass with a commercial
zero turn mower when he drove the mower under a parked semi truck trailer.  The
employee struck the trailer and became trapped, causing mechanical asphyxia and
multiple blunt force trauma injuries which killed him.
At 10:30 a.m. on August 7, 2020, an employee was travelling on a powered pallet
jack (industrial truck) from point A to point B through an aisle. The employee
attempted to squeeze through the aisle because there was another powered pallet
jack parked in the same aisle he was travelling on. The employee lost control as
he passed the parked pallet jack. The employee's pallet jack struck an adjacent
rack which pinned down his lower leg between the lower rack protector plate of
the rack system and the lower frame of the industrial truck he was operating.
The impact of his lower leg being pinned down resulted in a right lower leg
fracture.  The employee was hospitalized for treatment.
At 10:40 a.m. on April 18, 2021, an employee was working his first day for a
farm labor contractor as part of a crew of approximately 25 laborers picking
corn after dark in Westmorland, CA. The employee was resting between a tractor
and a connected trailer when the tractor operator, after securing boxes on the
trailer with rope, started the tractor to move the trailer to the side of the
road. As the tractor moved forward, the operator heard the employee scream and
immediately stopped. The employee sustained multiple fractures to the head, left
wrist, shoulder, left femur, and pelvis. Emergency services were called, and the
employee was transported to Desert Regional Medical Center in Palm Springs for
admission and treatment. The investigation determined that the employee was not
wearing a reflective vest as required for night work, and the tractor operator
did not ensure the area was clear before moving the vehicle.
At 12:33 a.m. on April 10, 2021, Employee #1, employed by a manufacturing
company, was removing dough from a catch pan inside the machine. The employee
reached behind a moving ram, which caught his hand, resulting in a crushing
injury. The employee was hospitalized for treatment.
At 12:58 p.m. on October 29, 2020, Employee #1, working as a construction
laborer, was drilling through a concrete wall using a power drill. While
operating the drill, the employee's gloved hand was caught in the rotating shaft
of the drill, resulting in a severe injury and amputation. Emergency services
were called to the scene, and the employee was transported to the hospital for
treatment. The employee was admitted and treated for the amputation injury.
At 12:05 p.m. on November 17, 2020, an employee was harvesting almonds. The
employee was the operator of a Jackrunner 400-180-T4F, and he was caught in a
jack rabbit (Wedge 10 Reservoir Cart). The employee had removed the safety
strips from his operator's door.  When he opened his door while the machine was
still running to troubleshoot a jam in the chain of the jack rabbit, he was
caught in the draper chain until another employee arrived and found him. The
employee admitted to removing the safety devices (for an unknown reason). EMS
arrived on scene and transported him to Memorial Medical Center in Modesto, CA.
He was treated and released the same day.  The employee suffered minor injuries,
including left ankle pain, a contusion of soft tissue, and blunt trauma to the
abdomen.
At 3:35 p.m. on November 2, 2020, an employee was putting away equipment after
deploying for a possible office building fire. A municipal bus ran over a hose,
pulling the hose.  The hose snapped off the fire truck's pump panel and struck
the back of the employee.  He fell to the ground, striking his head, and
sustained unspecified head trauma. He was hospitalized.
At 1:45 p.m. on April 19, 2021, an employee was walking around a corner when he
was struck by a stand-up pallet jack. The impact caused the load on the pallet
jack to fall, striking the employee. As a result, the employee sustained a
agency, but her supervisor was employed by the manufacturer. Both firms had
employees whose job title was operator or packer.
On February 7, 2021, an employee working as a manager for a dental implant
manufacturer called Coworker #1, dentist, to meet a client and a patient at his
dental clinic at 9:00 a.m. The client will use the clinic to televise a surgery
for training. Coworker #1 arrived at 8:56 a.m. and entered through the back door
where he noticed a floor opening. At 8:58 a.m., the client and patient arrived
at the front door. At 9:00 a.m., while waiting for the employee, they heard
moaning and investigated. They saw the employee laying below the floor. She had
come in the back door and fell through the 26-inch by 18-inch by 3-1/2-feet deep
opening. Coworker #1 pulled the employee out and called for an ambulance.
Coworker #2, building owner and clinic partner, said the employee texted him the
night before about meeting, but he did not see the text until this day. Coworker
#2 said Coworker #1 comes to the clinic unannounced every two weeks but never
when they are closed. Coworker #2 arrived to obtain signed liability agreements.
Coworker #2 said the construction company works in the building weekends
performing renovations. This day, they were replacing ventilation ducts below
the floor. Coworker #1 and Coworker #2 were puzzled why the employee came
he was standing on a caster mold cover to insert a tundish fly connector bar. A
later account said that he was placing a connecter into a mold. Some moisture
got into the mold. The instant transition from water to steam caused pieces of
molten steel to be thrown through the air. Some of the molten steel landed on
the employee. The employee suffered burns to his legs, a heel, his hands, and
the back of his head. He was hospitalized. The moisture that got into the mold
caused the melted steel to pop and injure the employee.
An employee delivered a package and was exposed to COVID-19.  The employee died
from complications from COVID-19 at approximately 5:30 p.m. on March 16, 2021.
At 9:15 a.m. on February 2, 2021, Employee #1 was engaged in rebuilding a
clarifier at a waste water treatment plant.  He was working from an extension
ladder and attempting to hook up a choker to a crane in order to rig a needed
part.  The employee lost balance and fell, striking the concrete floor, a fall
height of 9 feet.  He was transported to the hospital and admitted for treatment
of a fracture to his right leg.
At 12:45 a.m. on March 21, 2021, an employee was using a stationary disc grinder
to round a piece of metal he had fabricated. He tilted it to sand the burs off
the edges. The piece of metal flipped up, causing his finger to be caught
between the metal and disc grinder. The employee suffered a partial amputation
and was treated without hospitalization.
At 12:30 p.m. on March 26, 2021, Employee #1 was removing the center steel bands
securing four steel coils that were standing on end on a wooden pallet. The
coils were not centered on the pallet, and when the banding was cut, a
3,000-pound coil at the end of the pallet tipped over, striking Employee #1's
left foot. As a result, Employee #1 sustained a head laceration, a broken foot,
and a broken ankle. The foot was later amputated at the ankle.  Employee #1 was
hospitalized.
In early 2021, an employee was working at a general medical or surgical
hospital. He worked in the hospital administration and patient care areas. The
emergency department in particular was one place where he worked. On January 8,
2021, he was admitted to the hospital for COVID-19 after developing symptoms. On
January 13, 2021, he was discharged. The employer reported that there was no
breach in COVID-19 protocols and that the exposure was work-related.
At 5:09 p.m. on March 30, 2021, Employee #1 and Coworkers #1 and #2, employed by
a company engaged in construction traffic control, were installing a traffic
control sign.  Employee #1 was standing on the road between two stopped trucks,
one driven by Coworker #1 and the other driven by Coworker #2.  Coworker #1's
foot slipped off the truck's brake pedal and onto the accelerator pedal, which
caused the truck he was operating to move forward.  The truck struck Employee
#1, who was pinned between the two trucks.  Employee #1 sustained blunt force
traumatic crushing injuries.  Emergency medical services were called, and
Employee #1 was transported to the hospital, where he was pronounced dead.
In early 2021, an employee was working at a nursing care or skilled nursing
facility. He performed repairs and maintenance. For some reason, he contracted
COVID-19. At 10:00 a.m. on February 7, 2021, he died.
An employee was working as a nursing home administrator and normally performed
administrative tasks but he would routinely go to resident areas throughout the
work day to assist staff. On November 23, 2020, the employee  began feeling sick
with symptoms of COVID-19. The employee tested positive for COVID-19 on November
27, and was hospitalized on December 6, 2020. Prior to symptom onset, the
employee had been in close contact with a coworker who tested positive for
COVID-19 on November 19, 2020. No residents were known to be positive for
COVID-19 prior to the employee becoming symptomatic. Prior to the employee
becoming sick, he indicated that the PPE he was required to wear for COVID-19
protection was a surgical mask.
At 6:40 p.m. on January 26, 2021, Employee #1, a 54-year-old male newly assigned
to the stacker position, was removing plastic parts from a stacking machine. The
employee reached to retrieve a part that had fallen in the middle of the
stacker. During this process, the two halves of the stacker closed, creating a
pinch point and partially amputating the end of the employee's left third
finger. The employee was treated for his injury without hospitalization.
a fracture to his left forearm. He had no movement in his left-hand fingers and
wrist. He stayed in the hospital for 2.5 weeks.
At 12:45 p.m. on March 2, 2021, an employee (warehouse worker) of a meat,
seafood, and deli distributor was operating a Crown industrial truck (Serial No.
1A196600) in the warehouse when a piece of a broken wooden pallet became lodged
in its wheel. In an attempt to clear the obstruction, the employee stood his
foot out as a natural reaction. As a result, the employee's foot became stuck
between the industrial truck and a post, leading to a deep laceration on the
left foot. The employee was hospitalized for two weeks for treatment. No one
witnessed the accident, and the immediate supervisor was in his dock office at
the time. Cal/OSHA identified that the employee did not follow the correct
procedure for operating the forklift. No serious accident-related citations were
issued due to lack of employer knowledge.
At 1:30 p.m. on March 31, 2021, an employee was working as a machinist, was
wearing a rubber glove atop of a latex glove while operating Hardinge 2nd
Operation Chucker DV Five-Nine machine (Model # DV-59/DSM-59, Serial #
DV-59-19413). He was using 3M sandpaper to polish an aluminum C121-17 push-pull
tube. The push-pull tube was clamped to a rotating spindle. When he applied
additional pressure, his glove became tangled, and he attempted to pull his
glove. When the employee applied slightly more pressure while polishing the
aluminum C121-17 push-pull tube, his glove became tangled in the spindle. When
he tried to pull his glove, his thumb was caught in the process injuring his
right thumb. The employee was hospitalized for 4 days and lost his fingernail of
right thumb.
At 11:19 p.m. on July 23, 2020, an employee was demonstrating to a coworker how
to use and operate a brander in the production department of the rear production
hall. The employee inserted a plastic lid underneath the brander on top of the
anvil. As the employee was adjusting and aligning the lid on top of the anvil,
the coworker activated the two-touch hand control causing the brander head to
cycle downward and onto his right hand. The employee was hospitalized to treat a
fractured middle finger and a lacerated ring finger on his right hand.
At 8:45 a.m. on October 16, 2020, an employee working as a machine operator for
a motor vehicle parts manufacturer was standing on an elevated shaker table
using a rake to push parts into a bin. The employee slipped off the shaker table
and fell to the concrete ground below. The employee was hospitalized to treat a
fractured right leg and bruised right shoulder.
At 1:45 p.m. on March 5, 2021, Employee #1, a full-time maintenance worker at a
privately owned multifamily dwelling/condominium complex, was performing
preparatory work for painting. The employee was descending a 24-foot aluminum
extension ladder to retrieve painter's tape needed to secure plastic sheeting
over a window. While descending, the employee slipped and fell approximately 8
feet, sustaining a concussion and bruised ribs. Emergency services transported
the employee to Sharp Memorial Hospital for treatment and observation. The
employee was hospitalized for two days before being released.
At 1:30 p.m. on April 9, 2021, an employee was exiting a building under
construction when a forklift operator, who was backing up, struck the employee
with an all-terrain forklift (lull), pinning him against a concrete wall. The
employee sustained four fractured ribs, a laceration to the head, and internal
bleeding. Emergency services transported the employee to the hospital, where he
was admitted for treatment.
At 5:15 p.m. on November 2, 2020, an employee was working alone, operating a
rewinding machine. He was  holding an X-Acto knife in his right hand and
operating the rewinding machine with the safety gate/table in the down position.
When the X-Acto knife was caught between the primary roller and a roll of paper,
the employee lost his balance and tripped. The employee held on to the X-Acto
knife as it was pulled into the roller and the tip of his right index finger was
pinched between primary roller and the roll of paper. The employee sustained
lacerations on his fingertip and was treated without hospitalization.
At 1:30 p.m. on April 7, 2021, Employee #1 was preparing to replace the motor
drive of a feather separator machine when he fell approximately 8 feet 16 inches
to the concrete ground. Employee #1 sustained broken ribs, contusions, and a
laceration to the face. Emergency services transported the employee to the
hospital, where he was admitted and treated for his injuries.
At 2:30 p.m. on Thursday, March 18, 2021, an employee was working as a
production supervisor for a firm that manufactured corrugated and solid fiber
boxes. He was climbing a ladder to check the level in a tank. The ladder had
been placed on loose sand. It tipped over, causing the employee and the ladder
to fall. The employee landed on a concrete curb. He suffered fractured ribs. He
was hospitalized. The distance of the fall was not stated.
An employee was working in a skilled nursing facility when she was exposed to
residents and coworkers infected with COVID-19. The employee contracted COVID-19
and subsequently died from her infection at 12:30 p.m. on December 23, 2020.
At 2:30 p.m. on April 14, 2021, an employee was walking in the west parking lot
hours. Employee #1 sustained a fractured T6, lacerations to the face, nerve
damage in the jaw, and contusions to the legs.
An employee reported working on Monday, February 22, 2021.  The employee went
through the plant's COVID-19 screening process upon arriving at work.  The
employee did not register a fever and reported no symptoms during screening.
The employee worked from 7 a.m. to 11 a.m., doing his normal job as a shipping
supervisor, which included overseeing forklift operators on the shipping dock.
At 11 a.m., the employee said did not feel right, so he left work.  On Tuesday,
February 23, 2021, the employee went to see the doctor, who did a COVID-19 test,
and the test result came back positive.  The doctor sent the employee to the
family or duplex dwelling. It was a one-story building. The employee was
signaling a coworker who was lowering a concrete form rack into place. When the
coworker unhooked the crane from the rack, the rack fell on the employee. The
employee's neck was fractured. The employee was hospitalized.
At 9:00 a.m. on March 31, 2021, an employee finished stacking lumber and was
waiting for the forklift operator to remove the stack from the work area. For
unknown reasons, the employee crawled underneath an unguarded Corley board edger
and was struck in the head by the table saw blades and killed. A coworker stated
that he had told the employee to never to go under the edger when it was in
operation.
At 9:44 a.m. on April 2, 2021, an employee drove a company truck to a rail yard
located outside the facility. The employee walked for about 100 yard before he
sat down and rested and then collapsed. He pressed his radio distress button and
was later found by coworkers unresponsive. The employee's mouth was foaming and
clinched and he died before reaching the hospital.
At 11:14 a.m. on April 2, 2021, an employee was working on a "cut of cars" with
the engine approximately 700 feet behind him pushing ahead. The cut of cars was
supposed to proceed straight down the tunnel line, which required the employee
to align a specific switch with the tunnel. The employee radioed the engineer
and reported that the switch was in the proper position. The cut of cars left
the tunnel line and began to shift over to the wrong line where the employee was
riding. The engineer attempted to stop the cars, but couldn't. The employee was
caught between the cut of cars and the cars he was riding crushing his head and
killing him.
In late 2020, a seventy-three-year-old employee was working as a registered
nurse at a nursing care or skilled nursing facility. She was in charge of
infection control. She was exposed to the virus that causes COVID-19. On January
2, 2021, she tested positive for COVID-19. She was hospitalized on January 8,
2021. At 8:00 a.m. on January 27, 2021, she died.
At 3:15 a.m. on April 3, 2021, an employee blocking an obstruction on the
roadway while investigating an arrest when he was hit by an oncoming car. The
employee suffered multiple fractures and was killed.
At 12:00 p.m. on December 28, 2020, an employee was cleaning gutters at a
residential site when he lost balance and fell from the ladder. The fall
resulted in a fractured left ankle. The employee was hospitalized.
In late 2020, an employee was working as a licensed practical nurse (LPN) at an
assisted living facility for the elderly. She worked as a full-time night shift
nurse at the facility's station 1. She did not work on station 2, which was the
COVID-19 unit. She was a charge nurse. She oversaw certified nursing assistants
{CNAs) and made passes each night from 1:00 p.m. to 7:00 a.m., Monday through
Friday. She cared for approximately 25 residents. The director of nursing
revealed that there had been a COVID-19 outbreak at the facility. It had begun
on December 29, 2020. The employee had been in contact with other employees who
had tested positive. She had also been in contact with three of the infected
residents who had experienced no symptoms. On the employee's last day of work,
January 1, 2021, she did not indicate on the daily COVID-19 screening form that
she was experiencing any symptoms of COVID-19. Three days later, on January 4,
the employee arrived at the center and was tested in her vehicle by the director
of nursing. The employee reported to her work facility for a COVID-19 test but
remained in the car with her brother. She was experiencing symptoms of COVID-19,
such as coughing, at the time of testing. The center used a rapid antigen test,
which gave results within 15 minutes. The employee tested positive for COVID-19.
The director of nursing encouraged the employee to see her primary care
physician and to isolate for at least ten days. At 4:30 p.m. on January 13,
2021, the employee died.
At 5:15 a.m. on October 6, 2020, two employees were clearing a clogged chute,
removing coal and coal dust. A hot ember ignited, creating a flash fire.  Both
employees suffered burn injuries from the flash fire.  The employees were
treated without hospitalization.
At 10:09 a.m. on October 28. 2020, an employee working as an operator for a
plumbing and HVAC supplier was working with coworkers (also operators)
troubleshooting a die-electronic machine. The employee stuck his hand between
the machine and the die when the machine cycled. The employee received medical
treatment without hospitalization for an amputated left index fingertip.
At 10:40 p.m. on December 13, 2020, Employee #1, a Thermoformer machine/line
operator, was adjusting a machine-mounted fan that was positioned less than
seven feet from the walking surface. During the adjustment, Employee #1's left
middle finger came into contact with the moving fan blade, resulting in an
amputation of the first digit. Although the mounted fan was equipped with a
guard (shroud), the openings in the shroud were large enough for the employee's
fingers to pass through and make contact with the moving blades.  The employee
was hospitalized.   The incident occurred indoors, and weather conditions were
not a factor.
At 8:00 a.m. on March 30, 2021, an employee chased individuals (residents) that
ran away and escorted them back to campus. He followed one individual into his
room and there was a verbal and physical altercation where the resident swung
his arm/hand and struck the employee in the head. There was no noticeable injury
at the time, but the employee later died of an intracerebral hemorrhage.
At 9:15 a.m. on April 2, 2021, an employee was repairing an airline on a
coworker's semi truck when he he instructed the coworker to raise the fifth
wheel. The coworker got in the cab, revved up the engine, and noticed too late
that the truck moved forward enough to hit the other employee who was walking
between her truck and his truck's nose. The employee was caught between the two
trucks and killed.
In late 2020 or early 2021, an employee was working as an engineering technician
at a general medical or surgical hospital. This was a veterans' hospital. The
employee managed various HVAC projects throughout the hospital. It was possible
that he was exposed to COVID-19 on the job. He did have a confirmed personal
exposure to COVID-19 at home. At 9:00 a.m. on February 13, 2021, he died.
At 1:40 p.m. on March 16, 2021, Employee #1 was applying a spray coating to a
dump body unit when a lifting hook began slipping off the tailgate. As the
employee attempted to push the hook back into place, it detached completely,
causing the tailgate to shift and pinch the employee's finger. The incident
resulted in a finger amputation. Employee #1 was hospitalized for treatment.
At 2:20 p.m. on April 4, 2021, an employee was participating in felling a tree
and was using a chain saw over 40 feet up the tree. He was tied off to the tree
using a climbing belt and climbing spikes. A coworker was working as his
groundman holding a rope to lower section after he made a cut. After a
particular cut, a section fell suddenly due to tree rot and put a load on the
tree. The tree snapped below the employee causing him to fall to the ground as
the section landed on him. He suffered severe chest injuries and was killed.
At 8:50 a.m. on November 16, 2020, an employee was operating a Loopco slitter
machine. This machine processes a roll of sheet metal. A roll of sheet metal is
loaded onto a spindle, where it is uncoiled and fed into the slitter machine.
The machine then slits the metal to the desired size, and the strips are then
coiled onto a roll at the opposite end of the machine. The slitting action is
performed on rolls with blades attached, with spacers and rubber rolls that pull
the metal through the blades. At the time of the accident, the sheet metal that
was being processed was crinkling at the rolls. The employee was using a pipe to
raise the material at the infeed of the rolls and blades to prevent the metal
from crinkling as it was being cut. As the slitter was cutting the steel, the
employee was occasionally tapping the sheet metal to get it lifted as it was
being cut. As the employee did this, at one point the rolls grabbed the pipe and
the gloves the employee was wearing and pulled the left hand into the cutting
blades. The employee instinctively jerked his hand from the machine and then
felt a rush of blood. The worker ultimately sustained a total amputation of his
left wrist and hand. He was initially treated at San Joaquin County Hospital but
was later transferred to UC Davis Medical Center and hospitalized.
An employee was working for a specialized freight trucking company when he
tested positive for COVID-19 on March 5 , 2021. The employee was hospitalized on
March 17, 2021, and died due to his infection at 4:00 p.m. on March 28, 2021.
An employee was working at a plastics manufacturing facility when he contracted
COVID-19. The employee called in sick to work on March 14, 2021, and he died at
curtains pushing a heat sealer unit towards the drop curtains and forklift
driver.    The forklift struck the heat sealer unit that then struck the
employee causing unspecified injuries. The was killed the employee.
At 9:15 a.m. on May 19, 2021, an employee painted guidelines on pavement to
delineate an area to be milled. At some point, the employee was struck and
killed by a dump truck that began to back up.
At 6:00 a.m. on February 10, 2021, Employee #1 was using an Alpine Engineered
Products Inc. saw (model 645, Serial Number 645D03023-000) to cut lumber for
floor trusses. During operation, the saw blade became stuck. As the blade pulled
free, it struck the employee's left hand. The employee sustained an amputation
injury involving the little finger, ring finger, and half of the palm of the
left hand. Emergency services transported the employee to the hospital, where he
was admitted for treatment.
At approximately 10:00 a.m. on December 30, 2020, Employee #1, a landscaping
lead with over 40 years of experience, was operating a Walker MT riding
lawnmower with an attached deck, picking up leaves at a worksite. While seated
on the mower, he suddenly fell off, first onto the mower deck and then off the
left side of the machine. Although he was not struck or knocked off, he
speculated that he may have hit a rock or tree root, though he was uncertain.
Upon falling, his arm and leg were run over by the mower's tire, and he was
dragged until the mower came to a stop upon hitting a wall. Emergency services
transported him to the hospital, where he was admitted and treated for a
fractured leg requiring plate and screw insertions. He is currently in physical
therapy with an estimated recovery period of 6 to 8 months.
At 3:30 p.m. on February 10, 2021, Employee #1 was working for a machinery
moving contractor. Employee #1 was installing duct work in the Clean Room
ceiling. Employee #1 fell 9.5 feet to the ground. Employee #1 suffered fractured
legs and left shoulder.  Employee #1 was hospitalized.
An employee was working as facilities manager at a homeless shelter when he
contracted COVID-19 and required hospitalization for treatment of his infection
at 5:45 p.m. on December 16, 2020.
At 2:25 p.m. on November 30, 2020, an employee working as a postal clerk for the
United States Postal Service was walking to door #31 inside the PD&C loading
dock. The employee was walking alone preparing to receive a trailer that arrived
at the dock. The dock area is long and narrow measuring approximately 50 feet
wide and about 400 feet long. The employee had started at a desk by the facility
wall, walking along the dock doors, in close proximity to the doors. There was
no other clear path to the door due to pallets of mail filled the staging area.
A coworker operating a Toyota LP forklift was exiting a trailer backwards at
dock door #30. The coworker looked in the direction of travel and had the
back-up beeper sounding.  The employee saw the coworker exiting the trailer and
called out "stop, wait". The coworker did not hear or see the employee and
struck her. The employee amputated an unspecified number of toes and fractured
her hip, requiring hospitalization.
On November 27, 2020, an employee who worked as a back kitchen prep cook for a
delicatessen and restaurant lacerated and fractured her left index finger and
thumb.  The employee reached into the bowl of an unguarded food chopper through
the opening near the blade to remove chopped vegetables. She contacted the
rotating blade with her left hand and injured her index finger and thumb. The
employee's coworker (Supervisor) was in the area at the time and came to her
assistance. Another coworker transported the employee to the hospital for
treatment, where she was admitted.
At 3:00 p.m. on May 4, 2021, an employee working as a janitor for a food
manufacturer was cleaning the floor in the production area. The employee reached
under the ABL Pineapple Corer (Serial Number 3100A126) while it was stopped and
removed pineapple skins that were stuck in the machine. When the employee
removed the skins, the machine cycled and pulled the employee's right index
finger into the gears. The employee received medical treatment without
hospitalization for an amputated fingertip.
An employee was working in housekeeping at a nursing care or skilled nursing
facility. On April 22, 2021, during routine testing at work, she tested positive
for COVID-19. She was admitted to the hospital. She was on a ventilator until
she died at 1:30 p.m. on May 19, 2021.
At 3:15 p.m. on March 28, 2021, Employee #1 was operating a forklift when he
noticed bags jammed and ripped open on the conveyor line coming from the Avapac
2 section, heading toward the palletizer. While removing the bags from the
operating conveyor, Employee #1 was exposed to a cloud of powder in the air. As
he continued working, his right middle finger became caught in the conveyor
system. The employee was provided medical treatment and suffered the amputation
of the tip of his right middle finger just above the first knuckle.
Hospitalization was not required.
At approximately 2:45 p.m. on April 6, 2021, Employee #1 was operating a golf
cart while Employee #2 rode in the back to prevent an anteater from rolling off.
The anteater, which had been under anesthesia, awoke and began swinging its

An employee was working as a registered nurse for a temporary healthcare

At 10:20 a.m. on October 12, 2020, an employee working as a cashier for a farm
supply store was filling propane tanks at the propane dispensing station. After
filling each tank, the employee would shut down the nozzle to prevent propane
from pumping over the customer tank. The employee would then release the
pressure valve on the tank and discharge the line of the propane nozzle. The
employee was performing this propane tank-filling task and had just released
pressure after filling up a customer tank. After the employee finished filling
the tank and discharging the propane line, a loud ignition sound came from the
direction of the cabinet. The employee was struck by fire and burned. The
employee sustained second- and third-degree burns to her hands, arms and face
and was hospitalized.
At 12:45 p.m. on November 23, 2020, Employee #1 was trimming a tree branch while
working from a ladder approximately 14 feet above ground level. After the branch
was cut, it fell to the ground, bounced back, and struck the ladder. The
employee fell and sustained several broken ribs and a bruised back. Emergency
services transported the employee to the hospital, where he was admitted and
treated for the injuries.
At 12:45 p.m. on December 18, 2020, Employees #1 and #2, employed by a plumbing
company, were working inside a trench in preparation for installing a pipe at a
residential property.  They were leveling the ground inside the trench when a
trench wall collapsed.  Employee #1 was buried and fatally crushed by the
collapsing dirt.  Employee #1 was transported to the hospital and admitted for
treatment of injuries sustained in the trench collapse.
At approximately 11:15 a.m. on December 18, 2020, the employee was at home on a
weekend and became ill. The employee was admitted to the hospital with pneumonia
and COVID-19 illness.  The employee later died from complications of COVID-19.
At approximately 9:00 a.m. on December 15, 2020, an employee was cleaning snow
and ice from an employer-owned vehicle located in the employer's parking lot
adjacent to the highway. An electric distribution line runs parallel to the
highway, opposite the employer's parking lot.  An overhead branch line runs from
this distribution line, across the highway and continues across the employer's
parking lot to a pole-mounted transformer located at the rear of the parking
lot.  A tractor-trailer driving northbound on the highway struck and caught this
overhead power line which was hanging low due to snow and ice build-up on the
line.  The line was pulled tight then snapped loose from the transformer which
caused the line to whip across the parking lot.  The whipping line struck the
employee in the neck and killed the employee.
At 8:00 p.m. on November 18, 2020, Employees #1, #2 and #3 were working in and
around the seed storage house where cotton seed is stored after raw cotton is
taken through the ginning process. Employees #1, #2 and #3 smelled smoke and
noticed burnt material dropping into the bottom of the seed house. Employee #1
had burns to the hands, face, ears, and neck. Employee #1 had to be airlifted to
the hospital and was hospitalized. Employee #2 had burns to the left ear and
left hand and was hospitalized. Employee #3 had burns to the left hand and was
treated in the ER on an outpatient basis.
At approximately 12:00 a.m. on December 6, 2020, an employee a Registered Nurse,

treatments on scheduled shift, tube feedings, manage behaviors for demented
patients, communicating with providers, implementing orders, and  managing
crises as they occur on the shift.  The employee tested positive for COVID-19 on
November 23, 2020, and was subsequently quarantined. On November 23, 2020,
employee felt fine at the start of the work shift, but then notified the
supervisor that was not feeling well.  The employee was rapid-tested for
COVID-19 at work that day and tested positive.  On December 6, 2020, the

At approximately 8:20 a.m. on July 30, 2020, an employee was observing the
vegetable wash line, and saw the need to adjust the water flow line to the wash
line. The employee then climbed onto the rotating vegetable tumblers' level flat
metal bar which was flush with the unguarded rotating tumbler. The employee
inadvertently placed his right foot at the pinch point between a rotating
tumbler of the wash line and the standing platform while reaching the water
control valve that directed sprinkled water to the wash line. The tumbler cut
through the shoe and lacerated the employee's right toe; the employee was
hospitalized at Palomar Medical Center in Escondido and was advised that
amputation may be needed. The employee's supervisor was engaged in routine work
away from the wash line, and was generally aware of what each employee was
doing. At 6:17 a.m. on July 31, 2020, DOSH was notified by the employer, and
arrived on site at 10:30 a.m. on August 12, 2020.
At 12:30 p.m. on December 18, 2020, Employee #1 and a coworker were painting the
underside of a fabricated steel sled measuring approximately 6 feet wide, 20
feet long, and weighing around 6,000 pounds. To access the underside, they
attached the sled to a 10-ton overhead crane and lifted one end approximately 7
feet above the floor, leaving the other end resting on the ground. While
Employee #1 was underneath the suspended load painting, the crane cable broke,
causing the sled to fall onto Employee #1. The employee sustained a broken foot
and ankle, as well as a broken jaw.  The employee was hospitalized.
At 8:00 a.m. on November 17, 2020, an employee was attempting to diagnose
equipment malfunction.  The employee had disconnected a plug that he believed
supplied power to the motor. The employee placed a wrench on the equipment
shaft.  A motor started unexpectedly, causing the shaft and attached wrench to
rotate while the employee's hands were on the wrench.  The wrench struck a frame
member, and the employee's fingers were crushed between the wrench and frame.
The employee suffered multiple fractures to bilateral fingers and was
hospitalized.

into a 4-foot excavated hole.  He had been digging by hand to locate a pipe

was drilling holes in 2-1/2-inch by 2 1/2-inch square tube making a new post.
The employee was brushing the shavings off the tube when his leather glove
caught on the drill bit. The employee amputated his left pointer finger and
required medical treatment without hospitalization.
At approximately 9:45 a.m. on December 11, 2020, Employee #1, a male employee,
was on working surface while preparing the roof of a warehouse for
waterproofing. The warehouse roof was approximately 16.3 feet above the ground.
After exiting a 24-foot extension ladder, Employee #1 began to prep and clear
debris from the roof surface. Another coworker on the roof advised him to avoid
stepping on the skylights. However, Employee #1 stepped on a skylight, which
gave way, causing him to fall approximately 16.3 feet to the ground. The on-site
foreman immediately ran to assist the employee and instructed another coworker
to call 911. The Copley Fire Department arrived, stabilized Employee #1, and
transported him to a local hospital, where he was admitted for treatment of
serious injuries, including a broken leg and broken vertebrae.
At approximately 12:20 p.m. on January 2, 2021, an employee was working on the
rear left side of a garbage truck during a route. As the truck was driving down
a hill at approximately 20 mph, the employee leaned forward to access a backpack
on the handle, holding the grab bar with only one hand. The employee lost
balance and slipped off the back left step, falling onto the asphalt road. The
employee sustained head trauma, including cuts, contusions, and brain swelling.
The employee was hospitalized for treatment.
At 8:00 a.m. on October 12, 2020, an employee who worked as a Provider in a
hospital integrated practice unit (IPU) was hospitalized with COVID-19. The

narrative. The employer did not have an adequate respiratory protection program

At 8:15 a.m. on January 21, 2021, an employee working as a packer/stacker for a
food manufacturer was working on packaging machine 13. The employee had been
operating machine 12. Machine 13 had started up and had at least two instances
where the plastic packaging bunched up at the heat seal/knife area. The prior
two times the employee had stopped the machine to clear the jam. The third time
the employee did not stop the machine. The employee reached under the door
(interlocked guard) to clear the jam. The machine cycled and the jaws closed. As
the jaws closed, the employee's hand came into contact with the serrated blade.
The serrated knife lacerated the pad of his left thumb. The employee received
medical treatment without hospitalization for a lacerated thumb. The thumb pad
required later amputation due to the severity of the laceration.

a City Police Department was reported hospitalized with COVID-19. The employee
was actually hospitalized on November 20, 2020.  According to a coworker (Risk
Manager), on November 18, 2020, the employee and five coworkers, all Police
Officers including one Supervisor (Sergeant), were in a briefing room together
sitting around a single approximate 10 foot by 4 foot table. The employee and
coworkers wrote reports for approximately 6 hours.  At a certain times the
employees did not wear facial covers while talking to each other and while less
than six feet apart.  One of the coworkers had cold symptoms but continued to
work due to deadlines. Of the six Police Officers, three tested positive for
COVID-19. On November 20, 2020, the employee was off duty at a second home in
another City. That same day, he felt ill and was hospitalized for approximately
2 days due to COVID-19. The Union Representative stated that the Sergeant
thought the coworker was experiencing symptoms due to allergies.  The employer
did not have Adequate Aerosol Transmissible Diseases policies and procedures in
place.

location on the backflange, the employee began raising it. The backflange stuck
to the part underneath it and, when it broke free, bounced off the hook and
pinned the tip of the employee's left thumb between the backflange and the rack.

employee was treated without hospitalization.
